2.41.s:
vasuruvāca
athāvagāhanādīnāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalamucyate /
sāvadhānā śṛṇuṣva tvaṃ brahmaputri nṛpapriye //
2.41.d:
वसुरुवाच
अथावगाहनादीनां कर्मणां फलमुच्यते ।
सावधाना शृणुष्व त्वं ब्रह्मपुत्रि नृपप्रिये ॥
2.41.m: Vasu said: / Now the fruit of rites such as immersion is stated; / listen attentively, O daughter of Brahmā, O beloved of the king!

2.41.s:
yaiḥ puṇyavāhinī gaṅgā sakṛdbhaktyāvagāhitā /
teṣāṃ kulānāṃ lakṣaṃ tu bhavāttārayate śivā //
2.41.d:
यैः पुण्यवाहिनी गङ्गा सकृद्भक्त्यावगाहिता ।
तेषां कुलानां लक्षं तु भवात्तारयते शिवा ॥
2.41.m: By whom the merit-flowing Gaṅgā is bathed in even once with devotion, / auspicious [Gaṅgā] delivers a hundred thousand of their ancestral lines from worldly existence.

2.41.s:
sāmānyasthānato devi tatra saṃdhyā hyupāsitā /
puṇyaṃ lakṣaguṇaṃ kartuṃ samarthā dvijapāvanī //
2.41.d:
सामान्यस्थानतो देवि तत्र संध्या ह्युपासिता ।
पुण्यं लक्षगुणं कर्तुं समर्था द्विजपावनी ॥
2.41.m: Compared to an ordinary place, O goddess, the twilight prayer practiced there / is capable of making merit a hundred-thousandfold, purifying the twice-born.

2.41.s:
dattāḥ pitṛbhyo yatrāpastanayaiḥ śraddhayānvitaiḥ /
akṣayāṃ tu prakurvanti tṛptiṃ mohini durlabhām //
2.41.d:
दत्ताः पितृभ्यो यत्रापस्तनयैः श्रद्धयान्वितैः ।
अक्षयां तु प्रकुर्वन्ति तृप्तिं मोहिनि दुर्लभाम् ॥
2.41.m: Where waters are offered to the ancestors by sons endowed with faith, / they generate imperishable, hard-to-attain satisfaction, O Mohinī.

2.41.s:
yāvantaśca tilā martyārgṛhītāḥ pitṛkarmaṇi /
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi pitaraḥ svargavāsinaḥ //
2.41.d:
यावन्तश्च तिला मर्त्यार्गृहीताः पितृकर्मणि ।
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि पितरः स्वर्गवासिनः ॥
2.41.m: And as many sesame seeds as are taken by mortals in ancestral rites, / for that many thousands of years the ancestors dwell in heaven.

2.41.s:
pitṛlokeṣu ye kecitsarveṣāṃ pitaraḥ sthitāḥ /
tarpyamāṇāḥ parāṃ tṛptiṃ yānti gaṅgājalaiḥ śubhaiḥ //
2.41.d:
पितृलोकेषु ये केचित्सर्वेषां पितरः स्थिताः ।
तर्प्यमाणाः परां तृप्तिं यान्ति गङ्गाजलैः शुभैः ॥
2.41.m: Whatever ancestors of all people reside in the realms of the ancestors, / being gratified with the auspicious waters of the Gaṅgā, attain supreme satisfaction.

2.41.s:
ya icchetsaphalaṃ janma saṃtatiṃ vā śubhānane /
sa pitṝṃstarpayedgaṅgāmabhigamya surāṃstathā //
2.41.d:
य इच्छेत्सफलं जन्म संततिं वा शुभानने ।
स पितॄंस्तर्पयेद्गङ्गामभिगम्य सुरांस्तथा ॥
2.41.m: Whoever desires a fruitful birth or offspring, O fair-faced lady, / should approach the Gaṅgā and offer libations to the ancestors as well as to the gods.

2.41.s:
ye matā durgatā martyāstarpitāstatkulodbhavaiḥ /
kuśaistilairgāṅgajalaiste prayānti hareḥ padam //
2.41.d:
ये मता दुर्गता मर्त्यास्तर्पितास्तत्कुलोद्भवैः ।
कुशैस्तिलैर्गाङ्गजलैस्ते प्रयान्ति हरेः पदम् ॥
2.41.m: Those mortals who have died fallen into misfortune, when gratified by those born of their family / with kuśa grass, sesame seeds, and Gaṅgā water, go to the abode of Hari.

2.41.s:
svargasasthāśca ye kecitpitaraḥ puṇyaśīlinaḥ /
te tarpitā gāṅgajalairmokṣe yānti vidhervacaḥ //
2.41.d:
स्वर्गसस्थाश्च ये केचित्पितरः पुण्यशीलिनः ।
ते तर्पिता गाङ्गजलैर्मोक्षे यान्ति विधेर्वचः ॥
2.41.m: And whatever virtuous ancestors reside in heaven, / when gratified with Gaṅgā water, go to liberation: such is Brahmā's word.

2.41.s:
māsaṃ tarpaṇamātreṇa piṇḍasaṃpātanena ca /
gaṅgāyāṃ pitaraḥ sarve suprītāḥ sūryavarcasaḥ //
2.41.d:
मासं तर्पणमात्रेण पिण्डसंपातनेन च ।
गङ्गायां पितरः सर्वे सुप्रीताः सूर्यवर्चसः ॥
2.41.m: Merely by offering libations and presenting ancestral rice-balls for a month / in the Gaṅgā, all the ancestors become well-pleased, radiant like the sun.

2.41.s:
apsaro gaṇaṇasaṃyuktānhemaratnavibhūṣitān /
muktājālaparicchannānveṇuvīṇānināditān //
2.41.d:
अप्सरो गणणसंयुक्तान्हेमरत्नविभूषितान् ।
मुक्ताजालपरिच्छन्नान्वेणुवीणानिनादितान् ॥
2.41.m: Accompanied by hosts of apsarases, adorned with gold and jewels, / draped with nets of pearls, resplendent with the sounds of flutes and lutes,

2.41.s:
bherīśaṅkhamṛdaṅgādinirghoṣānsragvibhūṣitān /
gandharvadeharucirāndivyabhogasamanvitān //
2.41.d:
भेरीशङ्खमृदङ्गादिनिर्घोषान्स्रग्विभूषितान् ।
गन्धर्वदेहरुचिरान्दिव्यभोगसमन्वितान् ॥
2.41.m: having the sounds of kettledrums, conches, mṛdaṅga drums, and other instruments, adorned with garlands, / handsome with celestial bodies like gandharvas, endowed with divine enjoyments,

2.41.s:
āruhya tu vimānāgryānbrahyalokaṃ prayānti hi /
gaṅgāyāṃ tu naraḥ snātvā yo nityaṃ liṅgamarcayet //
2.41.d:
आरुह्य तु विमानाग्र्यान्ब्रह्यलोकं प्रयान्ति हि ।
गङ्गायां तु नरः स्नात्वा यो नित्यं लिङ्गमर्चयेत् ॥
2.41.m: mounting excellent celestial chariots, they go indeed to the world of Brahmā. / A person who, having bathed in the Gaṅgā, constantly worships the liṅga,

2.41.s:
ekena janmanā mokṣaṃ paramānpoti sa dhruvam /
agnihotrāṇi vedāśca yajñāśca bahudakṣiṇāḥ //
2.41.d:
एकेन जन्मना मोक्षं परमान्पोति स ध्रुवम् ।
अग्निहोत्राणि वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च बहुदक्षिणाः ॥
2.41.m: firmly attains supreme liberation in a single birth. / Agnihotra rites, the Vedas, and sacrifices with lavish priestly gifts

2.41.s:
gaṅgāyāṃ liṅgapūjāyāḥ koṭyaṃśenāpi no samāḥ /
pitṝnudiśya vā devāngaṅgāṃbhibhiḥ prasiṃcayet //
2.41.d:
गङ्गायां लिङ्गपूजायाः कोट्यंशेनापि नो समाः ।
पितॄनुदिश्य वा देवान्गङ्गांभिभिः प्रसिंचयेत् ॥
2.41.m: are not equal even to a ten-millionth part of the worship of a liṅga at the Gaṅgā. / Or, intending the ancestors or gods, one should sprinkle them with the waters of the Gaṅgā;

2.41.s:
tṛptāḥ syustasya pitaro narakasthāśca tatkṣaṇāt /
mṛtkuṃbhāttāmrakuṃbhaistu snānaṃ daśaguṇaṃ smṛtam //
2.41.d:
तृप्ताः स्युस्तस्य पितरो नरकस्थाश्च तत्क्षणात् ।
मृत्कुंभात्ताम्रकुंभैस्तु स्नानं दशगुणं स्मृतम् ॥
2.41.m: his ancestors, even if dwelling in hell, become instantly satisfied. / A bath [given] with copper pots is remembered as ten times [more meritorious] than from clay pots.

2.41.s:
raupyaiḥ śataguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ hemaiḥ koṭiguṇaṃ smṛtam /
evamarghe ca naivedye balipūjādiṣu kramāt //
2.41.d:
रौप्यैः शतगुणं पुण्यं हेमैः कोटिगुणं स्मृतम् ।
एवमर्घे च नैवेद्ये बलिपूजादिषु क्रमात् ॥
2.41.m: With silver [vessels, the merit] is remembered as a hundredfold; with gold [vessels], a ten-millionfold. / In the same manner, successively, with offerings of water, food offerings, offerings of oblations, and worship,

2.41.s:
pātrāṃ taraviśeṣeṇa phalaṃ caivottarottaram /
vibhave sati yo mohānna kuryādvidhivistaram //
2.41.d:
पात्रां तरविशेषेण फलं चैवोत्तरोत्तरम् ।
विभवे सति यो मोहान्न कुर्याद्विधिविस्तरम् ॥
2.41.m: The fruit increases ever more by virtue of the particular vessel. / If a person, having the means, through delusion does not perform the ritual with full elaboration,

2.41.s:
na sa tatkarmaphalabhāgdevadrohī prakīrtyate /
devānāṃ darśanaṃ puṇyaṃ darśanātsparśanaṃ varam //
2.41.d:
न स तत्कर्मफलभाग्देवद्रोही प्रकीर्त्यते ।
देवानां दर्शनं पुण्यं दर्शनात्स्पर्शनं वरम् ॥
2.41.m: He does not obtain the fruit of that rite, and is proclaimed an enemy of the gods. / Beholding the gods brings merit; better than beholding is touching [them].

2.41.s:
sparśanādarcanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ ghṛtasnānamataḥ param /
prāhurgaṅgājalaiḥ snānaṃ ghṛtasnānasamaṃ budhāḥ //
2.41.d:
स्पर्शनादर्चनं श्रेष्ठं घृतस्नानमतः परम् ।
प्राहुर्गङ्गाजलैः स्नानं घृतस्नानसमं बुधाः ॥
2.41.m: Higher than touching is worship; beyond this is bathing [them] with ghee. / The wise declare that bathing [them] with Gaṅgā water is equal to bathing [them] with ghee.

2.41.s:
arghyaṃ dravyaviśeṣeṇa gaṅgātoyena yaḥ sakṛt /
māgadhaprasthamātreṇa tāmrapātrasthitena ca //
2.41.d:
अर्घ्यं द्रव्यविशेषेण गङ्गातोयेन यः सकृत् ।
मागधप्रस्थमात्रेण ताम्रपात्रस्थितेन च ॥
2.41.m: If a person offers arghya even once with specific ingredients using Gaṅgā water, / measuring just a Māgadha prastha and placed in a copper vessel,

2.41.s:
devatābhyaḥ pradadyāttu svakīyapitṛbhiḥ saha /
putrapautraiśca saṃyuktaḥ sa ca vai svargamāpnuyāt /
āpaḥ kṣīraṃ kuśāgrāṇi ghṛtaṃ dadhi tathā madhu //
2.41.d:
देवताभ्यः प्रदद्यात्तु स्वकीयपितृभिः सह ।
पुत्रपौत्रैश्च संयुक्तः स च वै स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् ।
आपः क्षीरं कुशाग्राणि घृतं दधि तथा मधु ॥
2.41.m: To the deities along with his own ancestors, / he, joined by his sons and grandsons, reaches heaven indeed. / Water, milk, tips of kuśa grass, ghee, curd, and honey,

2.41.s:
raktāni karavīrāṇi tathā vai raktacandanam /
aṣṭāṅgaireṣa yuktor'gho bhānave parikīrtitaḥ //
2.41.d:
रक्तानि करवीराणि तथा वै रक्तचन्दनम् ।
अष्टाङ्गैरेष युक्तोर्ऽघो भानवे परिकीर्तितः ॥
2.41.m: Red oleanders, and likewise red sandalwood— / this arghya endowed with eight limbs is proclaimed for the sun.

2.41.s:
viṣṇoḥ śivasya sūryyasya durgāyā brahmaṇastathā /
gaṅgātīre pratiṣṭhāṃ tu yaḥ karoti narottamaḥ //
2.41.d:
विष्णोः शिवस्य सूर्य्यस्य दुर्गाया ब्रह्मणस्तथा ।
गङ्गातीरे प्रतिष्ठां तु यः करोति नरोत्तमः ॥
2.41.m: That best of men who performs the installation on the bank of the Gaṅgā / of Viṣṇu, Śiva, Sūrya, Durgā, or Brahmā,

2.41.s:
tathaivāyatanānyeṣāṃ kārayatyapi śaktitaḥ /
anyatīrtheṣu karaṇātkoṭiguṇaṃ bhavet //
2.41.d:
तथैवायतनान्येषां कारयत्यपि शक्तितः ।
अन्यतीर्थेषु करणात्कोटिगुणं भवेत् ॥
2.41.m: And likewise causes temples to be built for them according to his means, / [obtains] ten million times the merit of doing so at other sacred fords.

2.41.s:
gaṅgātīrasamudbhūtamṛdā ligāni śaktitaḥ /
salakṣaṇāni kṛtvā tu pratiṣṭhāpya dine dine //
2.41.d:
गङ्गातीरसमुद्भूतमृदा लिगानि शक्तितः ।
सलक्षणानि कृत्वा तु प्रतिष्ठाप्य दिने दिने ॥
2.41.m: Fashioning liṅgas according to his ability out of clay taken from the bank of the Gaṅgā, / equipped with all the proper marks, and having installed them day after day,

2.41.s:
mantreśca patrapuṣpādyaiḥ pūjayitvā ca śaktitaḥ /
gaṅgāyāṃ nikṣipennityaṃ tasya pupayamanantakam //
2.41.d:
मन्त्रेश्च पत्रपुष्पाद्यैः पूजयित्वा च शक्तितः ।
गङ्गायां निक्षिपेन्नित्यं तस्य पुपयमनन्तकम् ॥
2.41.m: And having worshipped them according to his capacity with mantras, leaves, flowers, and other offerings, / if he continually casts them into the Gaṅgā, his merit is endless.

2.41.s:
sarvānandapradāyinyāṃ gaṅgāyāṃ yo narottamaḥ /
aṣṭākṣaraṃ japedbhaktya muktistasya kare sthitā //
2.41.d:
सर्वानन्दप्रदायिन्यां गङ्गायां यो नरोत्तमः ।
अष्टाक्षरं जपेद्भक्त्य मुक्तिस्तस्य करे स्थिता ॥
2.41.m: That best of men who, in the Gaṅgā that bestows all joy, / recites with devotion the eight-syllable mantra—liberation rests in his hand.

2.41.s:
namo nārāyaṇāyeti praṇavādyaṃ niyamya ca /
ṣaṇmāsaṃ japataḥ sarvā hyupatiṣṭhanti siddhayaḥ //
2.41.d:
नमो नारायणायेति प्रणवाद्यं नियम्य च ।
षण्मासं जपतः सर्वा ह्युपतिष्ठन्ति सिद्धयः ॥
2.41.m: Controlling oneself and reciting for six months 'Oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya', / which begins with the praṇava, all supernatural powers attend upon him.

2.41.s:
namaḥ śivāyeti mantraṃ satāraṃ vidhinā tu yaḥ /
caturviśatilakṣaṃ vai japetsākṣātsaśaṅkaraḥ //
2.41.d:
नमः शिवायेति मन्त्रं सतारं विधिना तु यः ।
चतुर्विशतिलक्षं वै जपेत्साक्षात्सशङ्करः ॥
2.41.m: He who recites according to rule twenty-four hundred thousand times / the mantra 'namaḥ śivāya' with the tāra [Oṃ], is Śaṅkara in visible form.

2.41.s:
pañcākṣarī siddhavidyā śiva eva na saṃśayaḥ /
apavitraḥ pavitro vā japanniṣpātako bhavet //
2.41.d:
पञ्चाक्षरी सिद्धविद्या शिव एव न संशयः ।
अपवित्रः पवित्रो वा जपन्निष्पातको भवेत् ॥
2.41.m: The five-syllable mantra is a perfected knowledge; it is Śiva himself, without doubt. / Impure or pure, by reciting it one becomes free of sin.

2.41.s:
pūjitāyāṃ tu gaṅgāyāṃ pūjitāḥ sarva devatāḥ /
tasmātsarvaprayatnena pūjayedamarāpagām //
2.41.d:
पूजितायां तु गङ्गायां पूजिताः सर्व देवताः ।
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन पूजयेदमरापगाम् ॥
2.41.m: When the Gaṅgā is worshipped, all deities are worshipped; / therefore, with all effort, one should worship the river of the immortals.

2.41.s:
caturbhujāṃ trinetrāṃ ca sarvāvayavaśobhitām /
ratnakuṃbhasitāṃbhojavarābhayakaraṃ śubhām //
2.41.d:
चतुर्भुजां त्रिनेत्रां च सर्वावयवशोभिताम् ।
रत्नकुंभसितांभोजवराभयकरं शुभाम् ॥
2.41.m: Four-armed and three-eyed, adorned in all her limbs, / her hands holding a jeweled pitcher, a white lotus, and the gestures of bestowing boons and fearlessness, auspicious,

2.41.s:
śvetavastraparīdhānāṃ muktāmaṇivibhūṣitām /
suprasannāṃ suvadanāṃ karuṇārdrahṛdaṃbujām //
2.41.d:
श्वेतवस्त्रपरीधानां मुक्तामणिविभूषिताम् ।
सुप्रसन्नां सुवदनां करुणार्द्रहृदंबुजाम् ॥
2.41.m: Clothed in white garments, adorned with pearls and jewels, / very gracious, fair-faced, her lotus-heart moist with compassion,

2.41.s:
sudhāplāvitabhūpṛṣṭhāṃ trailokyanamitāṃ sadā /
dhyātvā jalamayīṃ gaṅgāṃ pūjayanpuṇyabhāgbhavet //
2.41.d:
सुधाप्लावितभूपृष्ठां त्रैलोक्यनमितां सदा ।
ध्यात्वा जलमयीं गङ्गां पूजयन्पुण्यभाग्भवेत् ॥
2.41.m: Inundating the surface of the earth with nectar, constantly bowed to by the three worlds— / meditating thus on the watery Gaṅgā and worshipping her, one becomes an inheritor of merit.

2.41.s:
māsārddhamapi yastvevaṃ nairantaryeṇa pūjayet /
sa eva devasadṛśo bahukāle phalādhikaḥ //
2.41.d:
मासार्द्धमपि यस्त्वेवं नैरन्तर्येण पूजयेत् ।
स एव देवसदृशो बहुकाले फलाधिकः ॥
2.41.m: Whoever worships her continuously in this manner even for half a month / becomes equal to a god, with even greater fruit over a long time.

2.41.s:
vaiśākhaśuklasaptamyāṃ jahnunā jāhnavī purā /
krodhātpītā punastyaktā karṇaraṅghrāttu dakṣiṇāt //
2.41.d:
वैशाखशुक्लसप्तम्यां जह्नुना जाह्नवी पुरा ।
क्रोधात्पीता पुनस्त्यक्ता कर्णरङ्घ्रात्तु दक्षिणात् ॥
2.41.m: Formerly, on the seventh day of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, the daughter of Jahnu [Gaṅgā] / was swallowed in anger by Jahnu, and released again from the cavity of his right ear.

2.41.s:
tāṃ tatra pūjayeddevīṃ gaṅgāṃ gaganamekhalām /
akṣayāyāṃ tu vaiśākhe kārtike 'pi śubhānane //
2.41.d:
तां तत्र पूजयेद्देवीं गङ्गां गगनमेखलाम् ।
अक्षयायां तु वैशाखे कार्तिके ऽपि शुभानने ॥
2.41.m: On that day, one should worship that goddess, the Gaṅgā whose girdle is the sky; / also on the Akṣaya [Tṛtīyā] in Vaiśākha, and in Kārtika as well, O fair-faced one.

2.41.s:
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā yavānnaiśca tilaistathā /
viṣṇuṃ gaṅgāṃ ca śaṃbhuṃ ca pūjayedbhakti bhāvataḥ //
2.41.d:
रात्रौ जागरणं कृत्वा यवान्नैश्च तिलैस्तथा ।
विष्णुं गङ्गां च शंभुं च पूजयेद्भक्ति भावतः ॥
2.41.m: Keeping vigil at night, with barley food and with sesamum seeds, / one should worship Viṣṇu, the Gaṅgā, and Śambhu with devotional feeling,

2.41.s:
tathā sugandhaiḥ kusumaiḥ kuṅkumāgarumandanaiḥ /
tulasībilvapatrādyairmātuluṅgaphalādibhiḥ //
2.41.d:
तथा सुगन्धैः कुसुमैः कुङ्कुमागरुमन्दनैः ।
तुलसीबिल्वपत्राद्यैर्मातुलुङ्गफलादिभिः ॥
2.41.m: As well as with fragrant blossoms, saffron, aloe wood, and sandal, / with tulasī and bilva leaves and the like, with citron fruits and other offerings,

2.41.s:
dhūpairdīpaiśca naivedyairyathā vibhavavistaraiḥ /
kalpakoṭisahasrāṇi kalpakoṭiśatāni ca //
2.41.d:
धूपैर्दीपैश्च नैवेद्यैर्यथा विभवविस्तरैः ।
कल्पकोटिसहस्राणि कल्पकोटिशतानि च ॥
2.41.m: With incense, lamps, and food offerings, according to the extent of one's means. / For thousands of tens of millions of kalpas and hundreds of tens of millions of kalpas,

2.41.s:
divyaṃ vimānamāsthāya viṣṇuloke mahīyate /
tato mahītalaṃ prāpya rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ //
2.41.d:
दिव्यं विमानमास्थाय विष्णुलोके महीयते ।
ततो महीतलं प्राप्य राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥
2.41.m: Mounting a celestial aerial chariot, he is honored in the world of Viṣṇu. / Then, returning to the earthly plane, he becomes a righteous king;

2.41.s:
bhuktvā vividhasaukhyāni rūpaśīlaguṇānvitaḥ /
dehānte jñānavānbhūtvā śivasāyujyamāpnuyāt //
2.41.d:
भुक्त्वा विविधसौख्यानि रूपशीलगुणान्वितः ।
देहान्ते ज्ञानवान्भूत्वा शिवसायुज्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
2.41.m: Having enjoyed various pleasures, endowed with beauty, good conduct, and virtues, / becoming enlightened at the end of the body, he attains union with Śiva.

2.41.s:
yajño dānaṃ tapo japyaṃ śrāddhaṃ ca surapūjanam /
gaṅgāyāṃ tu kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ koṭikoṭiguṇaṃ bhavet //
2.41.d:
यज्ञो दानं तपो जप्यं श्राद्धं च सुरपूजनम् ।
गङ्गायां तु कृतं सर्वं कोटिकोटिगुणं भवेत् ॥
2.41.m: Sacrifice, gift-giving, austerity, recitation, ancestral rites, and worship of the gods— / all performed at the Gaṅgā becomes multiplied tens of millions of times over.

2.41.s:
yastvakṣayatṛtīyāyāṃ gaṅgātīre dadāti vai /
ghṛtadhenuṃ vidhānena tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu //
2.41.d:
यस्त्वक्षयतृतीयायां गङ्गातीरे ददाति वै ।
घृतधेनुं विधानेन तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ॥
2.41.m: He who, on Akṣaya Tṛtīyā, gives away on the bank of the Gaṅgā / a cow made of ghee according to ritual rule—hear the meritorious fruit of that:

2.41.s:
kalpakoṭisahasrāṇi kalpakoṭiśatāni ca /
sahasrādityasaṃkāśaḥ sarvakāmasamanvitaḥ //
2.41.d:
कल्पकोटिसहस्राणि कल्पकोटिशतानि च ।
सहस्रादित्यसंकाशः सर्वकामसमन्वितः ॥
2.41.m: For thousands of tens of millions of kalpas and hundreds of tens of millions of kalpas, / radiant as a thousand suns and endowed with all desired objects,

2.41.s:
hemaratna maye citre vimāne haṃsabhūṣite /
svakīyapitṛbhiḥ sārddhaṃ brahmaloke mahīyate //
2.41.d:
हेमरत्न मये चित्रे विमाने हंसभूषिते ।
स्वकीयपितृभिः सार्द्धं ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
2.41.m: In a wonderful aerial chariot made of gold and jewels, adorned with swans, / he is honored in the world of Brahmā together with his own ancestors.

2.41.s:
tatastu jāyate vipro gaṅgātīre dhanānvitaḥ /
ante tu brahmavidbhūtvā mokṣamāpnotyasaṃśayaḥ //
2.41.d:
ततस्तु जायते विप्रो गङ्गातीरे धनान्वितः ।
अन्ते तु ब्रह्मविद्भूत्वा मोक्षमाप्नोत्यसंशयः ॥
2.41.m: Then he is born as a wealthy brāhmaṇa on the bank of the Gaṅgā; / at the end, having become a knower of Brahman, he attains liberation, without doubt.

2.41.s:
tathaiva gopradānaṃ ca vidhinā kurute tu yaḥ /
golomasaṃkhyavarṣāṇi svargaloke mahīyate //
2.41.d:
तथैव गोप्रदानं च विधिना कुरुते तु यः ।
गोलोमसंख्यवर्षाणि स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
2.41.m: Likewise, he who gives a cow according to ritual rule / is honored in the heavenly world for as many years as there are hairs on the cow.

2.41.s:
jāyate ca kule paścāddhanadhānyasamākule /
ratnakāñcanabhūpūrṇe śīlavidyāyaśonvite //
2.41.d:
जायते च कुले पश्चाद्धनधान्यसमाकुले ।
रत्नकाञ्चनभूपूर्णे शीलविद्यायशोन्विते ॥
2.41.m: Afterward, he is born in a family abundant in wealth and grain, / filled with jewels, gold, and lands, and endowed with good conduct, learning, and fame.

2.41.s:
sa bhuktvā vipulānbhogānputrapautrasamanvitaḥ /
mokṣabhāgī bhavennṛnaṃ nātrakāryā vicāraṇā //
2.41.d:
स भुक्त्वा विपुलान्भोगान्पुत्रपौत्रसमन्वितः ।
मोक्षभागी भवेन्नृनं नात्रकार्या विचारणा ॥
2.41.m: Having enjoyed immense pleasures together with sons and grandsons, / he will surely become an inheritor of liberation; there should be no doubt in this matter.

2.41.s:
kapilā yadi dattā syādvidhinā vedapārage /
narakasthānpitṝnsarvānsvargaṃ nayati vai tadā //
2.41.d:
कपिला यदि दत्ता स्याद्विधिना वेदपारगे ।
नरकस्थान्पितॄन्सर्वान्स्वर्गं नयति वै तदा ॥
2.41.m: If a brown cow is given according to ritual rule to one who has crossed over the Veda, / then he leads all his ancestors residing in hell to heaven.

2.41.s:
bhūmiṃ nivartanamitāṃ gaṅgātīre dadāti yaḥ /
bhūmireṇupramāṇābdaṃ brahmaviṣṇuśivātigaḥ //
2.41.d:
भूमिं निवर्तनमितां गङ्गातीरे ददाति यः ।
भूमिरेणुप्रमाणाब्दं ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवातिगः ॥
2.41.m: He who gives land measuring a nivartana on the bank of the Gaṅgā, / transcending Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva for as many years as there are dust particles of the earth,

2.41.s:
jāyate ca punarbhūmau saptadvīpapatirbhavet /
bherīśaṅkhādinirghoṣairgītavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ //
2.41.d:
जायते च पुनर्भूमौ सप्तद्वीपपतिर्भवेत् ।
भेरीशङ्खादिनिर्घोषैर्गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः ॥
2.41.m: Is born again on the earth and becomes the lord of the seven continents. / To the sounding of kettledrums, conches, and other instruments, and the melodies of vocal and instrumental music,

2.41.s:
stutibhirmāgaghānāṃ ca supto 'sau pratibudhyate /
sarvasaukhyānyavāpyeha sarvadharmaparāyaṇaḥ //
2.41.d:
स्तुतिभिर्मागघानां च सुप्तो ऽसौ प्रतिबुध्यते ।
सर्वसौख्यान्यवाप्येह सर्वधर्मपरायणः ॥
2.41.m: And to the eulogies of bards, he awakens from sleep. / Having attained all pleasures in this world and devoted to all righteousness,

2.41.s:
narakasthānpitṝnsarvānprāpayitvā divaṃ tathā /
svargasthitānmokṣayitvā svayaṃ jñānī ca mohini //
2.41.d:
नरकस्थान्पितॄन्सर्वान्प्रापयित्वा दिवं तथा ।
स्वर्गस्थितान्मोक्षयित्वा स्वयं ज्ञानी च मोहिनि ॥
2.41.m: Having caused all his ancestors residing in hell to reach heaven, / and causing those residing in heaven to attain liberation, himself enlightened, O Mohinī,

2.41.s:
ante jñānāsinā chitvā avidyāṃ pañcaparvikām /
paraṃ vairāgyamāpannaḥ paraṃ brahmādhi gacchati //
2.41.d:
अन्ते ज्ञानासिना छित्वा अविद्यां पञ्चपर्विकाम् ।
परं वैराग्यमापन्नः परं ब्रह्माधि गच्छति ॥
2.41.m: At the end, having severed with the sword of knowledge the five-knotted ignorance, / having attained supreme dispassion, he reaches the Supreme Brahman.

2.41.s:
saptahastena daṇḍena triṃśaddaṇḍā nivartanam /
tribhāgahīnaṃ gocarma mānamāha vidhiḥ svayam //
2.41.d:
सप्तहस्तेन दण्डेन त्रिंशद्दण्डा निवर्तनम् ।
त्रिभागहीनं गोचर्म मानमाह विधिः स्वयम् ॥
2.41.m: A rod measuring seven cubits—thirty such rods make a nivartana; / the ordinance itself declares a gocarma to be less by a third part [than that].

2.41.s:
grāmaṃ gaṅgātaṭe yo vai brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchati /
brahmaviṣṇuśivaprītye durgāyā bhāskarasya ca //
2.41.d:
ग्रामं गङ्गातटे यो वै ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयच्छति ।
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवप्रीत्ये दुर्गाया भास्करस्य च ॥
2.41.m: He who gives a village on the bank of the Gaṅgā to brāhmaṇas / for the pleasure of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Durgā, and the sun,

2.41.s:
sarvadāneṣu yatpuṇyaṃ sarvayajñeṣu yatphalam /
tapovrateṣu puṇyeṣu yatphalaṃ parikīrtitam //
2.41.d:
सर्वदानेषु यत्पुण्यं सर्वयज्ञेषु यत्फलम् ।
तपोव्रतेषु पुण्येषु यत्फलं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
2.41.m: Whatever merit exists in all gifts, whatever fruit in all sacrifices, / and whatever fruit is proclaimed in austerities and pious vows,

2.41.s:
sahasraguṇitaṃ tattu vijñeyaṃ grāmadāyinaḥ /
sūryakoṭipratīkāśe vimāne vaiṣṇave pure //
2.41.d:
सहस्रगुणितं तत्तु विज्ञेयं ग्रामदायिनः ।
सूर्यकोटिप्रतीकाशे विमाने वैष्णवे पुरे ॥
2.41.m: That is to be known as multiplied a thousandfold for the giver of a village. / In an aerial chariot resembling ten million suns, in the city of Viṣṇu

2.41.s:
krīḍate śāṅkare vāpi stuto devādibhirmudā /
bhūmireṇvabdasaṃkhyākaṃ kālaṃ sthitvā ca tatra saḥ //
2.41.d:
क्रीडते शाङ्करे वापि स्तुतो देवादिभिर्मुदा ।
भूमिरेण्वब्दसंख्याकं कालं स्थित्वा च तत्र सः ॥
2.41.m: Or in that of Śaṅkara, he disports, joyfully praised by the gods and others; / and having stayed there for a period equal in years to the dust particles of the earth,

2.41.s:
aṇimādiguṇairyukte yogināṃ jāyate kule /
akṣayāyāṃ tu yo devi svarṇaṃ ṣoḍaśamāsikam //
2.41.d:
अणिमादिगुणैर्युक्ते योगिनां जायते कुले ।
अक्षयायां तु यो देवि स्वर्णं षोडशमासिकम् ॥
2.41.m: He is born in a family of yogins endowed with the virtues of aṇimā and the other powers. / And whoever, on the Akṣaya [Tṛtīyā], O goddess, [gives] gold of sixteen māṣas,

2.41.s:
dadāti dvijamukhyāya so 'pi lokeṣu pūjyate /
annadānādviṣṇulokaṃ śaivaṃ vai tiladānataḥ //
2.41.d:
ददाति द्विजमुख्याय सो ऽपि लोकेषु पूज्यते ।
अन्नदानाद्विष्णुलोकं शैवं वै तिलदानतः ॥
2.41.m: Whoever gives [such gifts] to an eminent twice-born is also honored in the worlds. / From the gift of food [one attains] the realm of Viṣṇu, and the realm of Śiva from the gift of sesame seeds;

2.41.s:
brāhmaṃ ratnapradānena gohiraṇyena vāsavam /
gāndharvaṃ svarṇavāsobhiḥ kīrtiṃ kanyāpradānataḥ //
2.41.d:
ब्राह्मं रत्नप्रदानेन गोहिरण्येन वासवम् ।
गान्धर्वं स्वर्णवासोभिः कीर्तिं कन्याप्रदानतः ॥
2.41.m: the realm of Brahmā by the gift of gems; the realm of Indra by cattle and gold; / the realm of the gandharvas by gold and garments; renown by the gift of a maiden;

2.41.s:
vidyayā muktidaṃ jñānaṃ prāpya yāyānnirañjanam /
gaṃmātīre naro yastu nānāvṛkṣaiḥ samanvitam //
2.41.d:
विद्यया मुक्तिदं ज्ञानं प्राप्य यायान्निरञ्जनम् ।
गंमातीरे नरो यस्तु नानावृक्षैः समन्वितम् ॥
2.41.m: by sacred learning, having obtained liberation-giving knowledge, one will go to the taintless [Brahman]. / But that man who, on the bank of the Gaṅgā, [has made] a garden endowed with various trees,

2.41.s:
ārāmaṃ kārayedbhaktyā gṛhaṃ copavanānvitam /
kadalīnārikeraiśca kapitthāśokacaṃpakaiḥ //
2.41.d:
आरामं कारयेद्भक्त्या गृहं चोपवनान्वितम् ।
कदलीनारिकेरैश्च कपित्थाशोकचंपकैः ॥
2.41.m: or with devotion causes a grove to be made, or a house endowed with a park, / having plantains, coconuts, wood-apples, aśokas, and campakas,

2.41.s:
panasairbilvavṛkṣaiśca kadaṃbāśvatthapāṭalaiḥ /
āmraistālairnāgaraṅgairvṛkṣairanyaiśca saṃyutam //
2.41.d:
पनसैर्बिल्ववृक्षैश्च कदंबाश्वत्थपाटलैः ।
आम्रैस्तालैर्नागरङ्गैर्वृक्षैरन्यैश्च संयुतम् ॥
2.41.m: jackfruits, bilva trees, kadambas, aśvatthas, and pāṭalas, / together with mangoes, palmyras, oranges, and other trees,

2.41.s:
jātīvijayasaṃyuktaṃ tathā pāṭalarājitam /
nicitaṃ kārayitvaivamāvāsaṃ puṣpaśobhitam //
2.41.d:
जातीविजयसंयुक्तं तथा पाटलराजितम् ।
निचितं कारयित्वैवमावासं पुष्पशोभितम् ॥
2.41.m: endowed with jasmine and vijayā, and shining with pāṭala flowers— / having thus caused a dwelling covered and adorned with flowers to be constructed,

2.41.s:
śivāya viṣṇave vāpi durgāyai bhāskarāya ca /
prayacchati tathā bhaktyā sarvārthaṃ parikalpya ca //
2.41.d:
शिवाय विष्णवे वापि दुर्गायै भास्कराय च ।
प्रयच्छति तथा भक्त्या सर्वार्थं परिकल्प्य च ॥
2.41.m: he offers it with devotion to Śiva, or to Viṣṇu, / or to Durgā, or to the Sun, intending it for all purposes.

2.41.s:
tasya puṇyaphalaṃ vakṣye saṃkṣepānnatu vistarāt /
yāvanti teṣāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ puṣpamūlaphalāni ca //
2.41.d:
तस्य पुण्यफलं वक्ष्ये संक्षेपान्नतु विस्तरात् ।
यावन्ति तेषां वृक्षाणां पुष्पमूलफलानि च ॥
2.41.m: I shall state the fruit of his merit in brief, not in detail: / as many flowers, roots, and fruits as those trees have,

2.41.s:
bījāni ca vicitrāṇi teṣāṃ mūlāni vai tathā /
tāvatkalpasahasrāṇi teṣāṃ lokeṣu saṃsthitiḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge mohinīvasusaṃvāde gaṅgāmāhātmye dānādividhivarṇanaṃ nāmaikacatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.41.d:
बीजानि च विचित्राणि तेषां मूलानि वै तथा ।
तावत्कल्पसहस्राणि तेषां लोकेषु संस्थितिः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे मोहिनीवसुसंवादे गङ्गामाहात्म्ये दानादिविधिवर्णनं नामैकचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
2.41.m:
and as many diverse seeds and roots as they possess, / for that many thousands of kalpas is his dwelling in their worlds.

Thus ends the forty-first chapter, entitled "The Description of the Rules of Gifts and Other Rites" in the Eulogy of the Greatness of the Gaṅgā, in the conversation between Mohinī and Vasu in the latter part of the illustrious Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

2.42.s:
mohinyuvāca
dhanyāhaṃ kṛtakṛtyāhaṃ saphalaṃ jīvitaṃ mama /
yacchrutaṃ tvanmukhāṃbhojādgāmāhātmyamuttamam //
2.42.d:
मोहिन्युवाच
धन्याहं कृतकृत्याहं सफलं जीवितं मम ।
यच्छ्रुतं त्वन्मुखांभोजाद्गामाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ॥
2.42.m: Mohinī said: / Blessed am I, fulfilled am I, fruitful is my life, / since the supreme eulogy of the greatness of the Gaṅgā has been heard from your lotus-mouth!

2.42.s:
aho gaṅgāsamaṃ tīrthaṃ nāsti kiñciddharā tale /
yasyāḥ saṃdarśanādīnāmīdṛśaṃ puṇyamīritam //
2.42.d:
अहो गङ्गासमं तीर्थं नास्ति किञ्चिद्धरा तले ।
यस्याः संदर्शनादीनामीदृशं पुण्यमीरितम् ॥
2.42.m: Ah, there is no sacred ford equal to the Gaṅgā anywhere on the face of the earth, / the sight and other acts regarding which have such merit declared [of them]!

2.42.s:
guḍadhenvādidhenūnāṃ vidhānaṃ ca yathākramam /
tathā kathayaviprendra bhaktāhaṃ tava sarvadā //
2.42.d:
गुडधेन्वादिधेनूनां विधानं च यथाक्रमम् ।
तथा कथयविप्रेन्द्र भक्ताहं तव सर्वदा ॥
2.42.m: Explain also the ritual procedure for the molasses-cow and other [symbolic] cows in proper order, / O best of brahmins; I am ever your devotee.

2.42.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
tacchrutvā mohinīvākyaṃ vasustasyāḥ purohitaḥ /
vedāgamānāṃ tattvajñaḥ smayamāna uvāca ha //
2.42.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
तच्छ्रुत्वा मोहिनीवाक्यं वसुस्तस्याः पुरोहितः ।
वेदागमानां तत्त्वज्ञः स्मयमान उवाच ह ॥
2.42.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Having heard those words of Mohinī, Vasu, her family priest, / who knew the true meaning of the Vedas and Āgamas, smiled and said:

2.42.s:
vasuruvāca
śṛṇu mohini vakṣyāmi yatpṛṣṭaṃ hi tvayā mama /
guḍadhenuvidhānaṃ ca yathā śāstre prakīrtitam //
2.42.d:
वसुरुवाच
शृणु मोहिनि वक्ष्यामि यत्पृष्टं हि त्वया मम ।
गुडधेनुविधानं च यथा शास्त्रे प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
2.42.m: Vasu said: / Listen, O Mohinī, I will explain what has indeed been asked by you of me: / the ritual procedure for the molasses-cow, as it is proclaimed in the scripture.

2.42.s:
kṛṣṇājinaṃ caturgrīvaṃ vinyasedbhuvi /
gomayenopaliptāyāṃ kuśānāstīrya yatnataḥ //
2.42.d:
कृष्णाजिनं चतुर्ग्रीवं विन्यसेद्भुवि ।
गोमयेनोपलिप्तायां कुशानास्तीर्य यत्नतः ॥
2.42.m: One should place a black antelope skin with four necks upon the ground / that has been smeared with cow dung, having carefully spread kuśa grass [thereon].

2.42.s:
praṅmukhīṃ kalpayeddhenumudakpādāṃ savatsakām /
uttamā guḍadhenustu caturbhāraiḥ prakīrtitā //
2.42.d:
प्रङ्मुखीं कल्पयेद्धेनुमुदक्पादां सवत्सकाम् ।
उत्तमा गुडधेनुस्तु चतुर्भारैः प्रकीर्तिता ॥
2.42.m: One should fashion the cow facing east, with feet directed north, along with her calf. / An excellent molasses-cow is proclaimed to be made of four bhāras [of molasses];

2.42.s:
vatsaṃ bhāreṇa kurvīta bhārābhyāṃ madhyamā smṛtā /
arddhabhāreṇa vatsaḥ syātkaniṣṭhā bhārakeṇa tu //
2.42.d:
वत्सं भारेण कुर्वीत भाराभ्यां मध्यमा स्मृता ।
अर्द्धभारेण वत्सः स्यात्कनिष्ठा भारकेण तु ॥
2.42.m: one should make the calf with one bhāra; a medium one is considered to be of two bhāras, / and the calf should be half a bhāra; but the lowest is made of one bhāra,

2.42.s:
caturthāṃśena vatsaḥ syād gṛhavittānusārataḥ /
prabhuḥ prathamakalpasya yo 'nukalpena vartayet //
2.42.d:
चतुर्थांशेन वत्सः स्याद् गृहवित्तानुसारतः ।
प्रभुः प्रथमकल्पस्य यो ऽनुकल्पेन वर्तयेत् ॥
2.42.m: and the calf should be one-fourth [of a bhāra], according to the wealth of one's household. / A capable person who, [instead] of the primary rule, acts according to a secondary rule,

2.42.s:
na sāṃparāyikaṃ tasya durmaterjāyate phalam /
dhenuvatsau ghṛtasyaitau sitaślakṣṇāṃbarāvṛtau //
2.42.d:
न सांपरायिकं तस्य दुर्मतेर्जायते फलम् ।
धेनुवत्सौ घृतस्यैतौ सितश्लक्ष्णांबरावृतौ ॥
2.42.m: to that foolish person no fruit concerning the hereafter accrues. / These two, the cow and calf of ghee, should be covered with white, fine cloths,

2.42.s:
śuktikarṇāvikṣupādau śuddhamuktālekṣaṇau /
sitasūtraśirālau ca sitakaṃbalakaṃbalau //
2.42.d:
शुक्तिकर्णाविक्षुपादौ शुद्धमुक्तालेक्षणौ ।
सितसूत्रशिरालौ च सितकंबलकंबलौ ॥
2.42.m: with pearl oysters for ears, sugarcane for legs, pure pearls for eyes, / white threads for veins, and white blankets for dewlaps,

2.42.s:
tāmragaṇḍūkapṛṣṭhau tau sitacāmaralomakau /
vidrumakramago petau navanītastanānvitau //
2.42.d:
ताम्रगण्डूकपृष्ठौ तौ सितचामरलोमकौ ।
विद्रुमक्रमगो पेतौ नवनीतस्तनान्वितौ ॥
2.42.m: with copper vessels for their backs, white chowries for hair, / provided with corals for brow-ridges, and endowed with butter for udders,

2.42.s:
kāṃsyadohāvindranīlamaṇikalpitatārakau /
suvarṇaśṛṅgābharaṇau śuddharaupyakhurāvubhau //
2.42.d:
कांस्यदोहाविन्द्रनीलमणिकल्पिततारकौ ।
सुवर्णशृङ्गाभरणौ शुद्धरौप्यखुरावुभौ ॥
2.42.m: with bell-metal vessels for milking, with pupils fashioned of sapphires, / both having gold ornaments for horns, and pure silver for hooves,

2.42.s:
nānāphalaṃ samāyuktau ghrāṇagandhakaraṇḍakau /
ityevaṃ racayitvā tu dhūpadīpairathārcayet //
2.42.d:
नानाफलं समायुक्तौ घ्राणगन्धकरण्डकौ ।
इत्येवं रचयित्वा तु धूपदीपैरथार्चयेत् ॥
2.42.m: provided with various fruits, with fragrance-boxes for the organ of smell. / Having thus fashioned [them], one should then worship them with incense and lamps:

2.42.s:
yā lakṣmīḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yā ca deveṣvavasthitā /
dhenurūpeṇa sā devī mama śāntiṃ prayacchatu //
2.42.d:
या लक्ष्मीः सर्वभूतानां या च देवेष्ववस्थिता ।
धेनुरूपेण सा देवी मम शान्तिं प्रयच्छतु ॥
2.42.m: "May that goddess Lakṣmī who is in all beings and who abides in the gods, / in the form of a cow, grant peace to me!"

2.42.s:
dehasthā yā ca rudrāṇāṃ śaṅkarasya sadā priyā /
dhenurūpeṇa sā devī mama pāpaṃ vyapohatu //
2.42.d:
देहस्था या च रुद्राणां शङ्करस्य सदा प्रिया ।
धेनुरूपेण सा देवी मम पापं व्यपोहतु ॥
2.42.m: And the goddess who resides in the bodies of the Rudras, ever beloved of Śaṅkara, / may she, in the form of a cow, dispel my sin.

2.42.s:
viṣṇorvakṣasi yā lakṣmīḥ svāhārūpā vibhāvasoḥ /
candrārkaśakraśaktiryā dhenurūpāstu sā śriye //
2.42.d:
विष्णोर्वक्षसि या लक्ष्मीः स्वाहारूपा विभावसोः ।
चन्द्रार्कशक्रशक्तिर्या धेनुरूपास्तु सा श्रिये ॥
2.42.m: The Lakṣmī who rests on Viṣṇu's chest, who is the Svāhā of the fire, / who is the power of the Moon, the Sun, and Śakra—may she, in the form of a cow, bring prosperity.

2.42.s:
caturmukhasya yā lakṣmīrlakṣmīryā dhanadasya ca /
lakṣmīryā lokapālānāṃ sā dhenurvaradāstu me //
2.42.d:
चतुर्मुखस्य या लक्ष्मीर्लक्ष्मीर्या धनदस्य च ।
लक्ष्मीर्या लोकपालानां सा धेनुर्वरदास्तु मे ॥
2.42.m: The Lakṣmī of the Four-faced [Brahmā], and the Lakṣmī of the giver of wealth [Kubera], / the Lakṣmī of the guardians of the directions—may that cow grant me boons.

2.42.s:
svadhā yā pitṛmukhyānāṃ svāhā yajñamujā ca yā /
sarvapāpaharā dhenuḥ sā me śāntiṃ prayacchatu //
2.42.d:
स्वधा या पितृमुख्यानां स्वाहा यज्ञमुजा च या ।
सर्वपापहरा धेनुः सा मे शान्तिं प्रयच्छतु ॥
2.42.m: She who is Svadhā to the foremost ancestors, and she who is Svāhā to the enjoyers of sacrifice— / may that cow, the destroyer of all sins, grant me peace.

2.42.s:
evamāṃmatrya tāṃ dhenuṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet /
vidhānametaddhenūnāṃ sarvāsāmiha paṭhyate //
2.42.d:
एवमांमत्र्य तां धेनुं ब्राह्मणाय निवेदयेत् ।
विधानमेतद्धेनूनां सर्वासामिह पठ्यते ॥
2.42.m: Having thus consecrated that cow, he should offer it to a brāhmaṇa. / This procedure is recited here for all [symbolic] cows.

2.42.s:
yāstu pāparvināśinyaḥ kīrtitā daśadhenavaḥ /
tāsāṃ svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi śāstrokaṃ śṛṇu mohini //
2.42.d:
यास्तु पापर्विनाशिन्यः कीर्तिता दशधेनवः ।
तासां स्वरूपं वक्ष्यामि शास्त्रोकं शृणु मोहिनि ॥
2.42.m: The ten cows that are celebrated as destroyers of sins— / listen, O Mohinī, to their true nature as taught in scripture.

2.42.s:
prathamā guḍadhenuḥ syād ghṛtadhenurathāparā /
tiladhenustṛtīyā ca caturthī jalasaṃjñitā //
2.42.d:
प्रथमा गुडधेनुः स्याद् घृतधेनुरथापरा ।
तिलधेनुस्तृतीया च चतुर्थी जलसंज्ञिता ॥
2.42.m: The first is the jaggery-cow, and the second is the ghee-cow; / the third is the sesame-cow, and the fourth is designated as the water-cow.

2.42.s:
pañcamī kṣīradhenuśca ṣaṣṭhī madhumayī smṛtā /
saptamī śarkarādhenurdadhidhenustathāṣṭamī //
2.42.d:
पञ्चमी क्षीरधेनुश्च षष्ठी मधुमयी स्मृता ।
सप्तमी शर्कराधेनुर्दधिधेनुस्तथाष्टमी ॥
2.42.m: The fifth is the milk-cow, and the sixth is remembered as made of honey; / the seventh is the sugar-cow, and likewise the eighth is the curd-cow.

2.42.s:
ratnadhenuśca navamī daśamī tu svarūpataḥ /
kuṃbhāḥ syurdravadhenūnāṃ cetarāsāṃ tu rāśayaḥ //
2.42.d:
रत्नधेनुश्च नवमी दशमी तु स्वरूपतः ।
कुंभाः स्युर्द्रवधेनूनां चेतरासां तु राशयः ॥
2.42.m: The ninth is the jewel-cow, and the tenth is in its true form [gold]; / jars are [used] for the liquid-cows, while heaps [are used] for the others.

2.42.s:
survaṇadhenumapyatra kecidicchanti sūrayaḥ /
navanītena tailena tathā ke 'pi maharṣayaḥ //
2.42.d:
सुर्वणधेनुमप्यत्र केचिदिच्छन्ति सूरयः ।
नवनीतेन तैलेन तथा के ऽपि महर्षयः ॥
2.42.m: Here, some wise men also accept a gold-cow, / and likewise some great sages [accept cows made] of butter and oil.

2.42.s:
etadeva vidhānaṃ syādeta eva hyupaskarāḥ /
mantrāvāhanasaṃyuktāḥ sadā parvaṇi parvaṇi //
2.42.d:
एतदेव विधानं स्यादेत एव ह्युपस्कराः ।
मन्त्रावाहनसंयुक्ताः सदा पर्वणि पर्वणि ॥
2.42.m: The rite itself is the same, and these very accessories are used, / accompanied by mantras and invocations, always on each sacred occasion.

2.42.s:
yathāśraddhaṃ pradātavyā bhuktimuktiphalapradāḥ /
anekayajñaphaladāḥ sarvapāpaharāḥ śubhāḥ //
2.42.d:
यथाश्रद्धं प्रदातव्या भुक्तिमुक्तिफलप्रदाः ।
अनेकयज्ञफलदाः सर्वपापहराः शुभाः ॥
2.42.m: They should be given according to one's faith, granting the fruits of enjoyment and liberation, / bestowing the fruits of many sacrifices, auspicious and removing all sins,

2.42.s:
ayane viṣuve puṇye vyatīpāte 'thavā punaḥ /
yugādau caiva manvādau coparāgādiparvasu //
2.42.d:
अयने विषुवे पुण्ये व्यतीपाते ऽथवा पुनः ।
युगादौ चैव मन्वादौ चोपरागादिपर्वसु ॥
2.42.m: at the solstice, at the holy equinox, or at a Vyatīpāta, / at the start of a Yuga, at the start of a Manvantara, and on sacred occasions such as an eclipse.

2.42.s:
guḍadhenvādayo deyā bhaktiśraddhāsamanvitaiḥ /
tīrtheṣu svagṛhe vāpi gaṅgātīre viśeṣataḥ //
2.42.d:
गुडधेन्वादयो देया भक्तिश्रद्धासमन्वितैः ।
तीर्थेषु स्वगृहे वापि गङ्गातीरे विशेषतः ॥
2.42.m: Endowed with devotion and faith, one should give the jaggery-cow and others / at sacred fords or in one's own house, especially on the bank of the Gaṅgā.

2.42.s:
evaṃ datvā vidhānena dhenuṃ dvijavarāya ca /
pradakṣiṇīkṛtya vipraṃ dakṣiṇābhiḥ pratoṣya ca //
2.42.d:
एवं दत्वा विधानेन धेनुं द्विजवराय च ।
प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य विप्रं दक्षिणाभिः प्रतोष्य च ॥
2.42.m: Having thus given the cow according to the rule to an excellent twice-born, / circumambulating the brāhmaṇa and satisfying him with fees,

2.42.s:
ṛtvijaḥ prītisaṃyukto namaskṛtya visarjayet /
tataḥ saṃpūjayedgaṅgāṃ vidhinā susamāhitaḥ //
2.42.d:
ऋत्विजः प्रीतिसंयुक्तो नमस्कृत्य विसर्जयेत् ।
ततः संपूजयेद्गङ्गां विधिना सुसमाहितः ॥
2.42.m: filled with affection, one should bow to the officiating priests and dismiss them. / Then, well concentrated, one should worship the Gaṅgā according to the rule.

2.42.s:
aṣṭamūrtidharāṃ devīṃ divyarūpāṃ nirīkṣya ca /
śālitandulaprasthena dviprasthapayasā tathā //
2.42.d:
अष्टमूर्तिधरां देवीं दिव्यरूपां निरीक्ष्य च ।
शालितन्दुलप्रस्थेन द्विप्रस्थपयसा तथा ॥
2.42.m: Looking upon the goddess of divine form, who assumes the eight forms, / with a prastha of Śāli rice and two prasthas of milk,

2.42.s:
pāyasaṃ kārayitvā ca datvā madhu ghṛtaṃ tathā /
pratyekaṃ palamātraṃ ca bhaktibhāvena saṃyutaḥ //
2.42.d:
पायसं कारयित्वा च दत्वा मधु घृतं तथा ।
प्रत्येकं पलमात्रं च भक्तिभावेन संयुतः ॥
2.42.m: having milk-porridge prepared and adding honey and ghee, / a pala's weight of each, filled with devotional feeling,

2.42.s:
tatpāyasamapūpāṃśca modakā maṇḍalāni ca /
tathā guñjārddhamātraṃ ca suvarṇaṃ rūpyameva ca //
2.42.d:
तत्पायसमपूपांश्च मोदका मण्डलानि च ।
तथा गुञ्जार्द्धमात्रं च सुवर्णं रूप्यमेव च ॥
2.42.m: that milk-porridge, cakes, modakas, and sweetmeats, / as well as gold and silver of the weight of half a guñjā,

2.42.s:
candanāgarukarpūrakuṅkumāni ca guggulam /
bilvapatrāṇi dūrvāśca rocanā sitacandanam //
2.42.d:
चन्दनागरुकर्पूरकुङ्कुमानि च गुग्गुलम् ।
बिल्वपत्राणि दूर्वाश्च रोचना सितचन्दनम् ॥
2.42.m: sandalwood, agarwood, camphor, saffron, and guggulu, / bael leaves, dūrvā grass, rocanā, and white sandalwood,

2.42.s:
nīlotpalāni cānyāni puṣpāṇi surabhīṇi ca /
yathāśakti mahābhaktyā gaṅgāyāṃ caiva nikṣipet //
2.42.d:
नीलोत्पलानि चान्यानि पुष्पाणि सुरभीणि च ।
यथाशक्ति महाभक्त्या गङ्गायां चैव निक्षिपेत् ॥
2.42.m: blue lotuses and other fragrant flowers, / one should cast into the Gaṅgā with great devotion according to one's means,

2.42.s:
mantreṇānena subhage purāṇoktena cāpi hi /
oṅgaṅgāyai nārāyaṇyai śivāyai ca namonamaḥ //
2.42.d:
मन्त्रेणानेन सुभगे पुराणोक्तेन चापि हि ।
ओङ्गङ्गायै नारायण्यै शिवायै च नमोनमः ॥
2.42.m: and also with this mantra taught in the Purāṇas, O lovely woman: / 'Oṃ, to Gaṅgā, to Nārāyaṇī, to Śivā, homage, homage!'

2.42.s:
etadeva vidhānaṃ tu māsi māsi ca mohini /
paurṇamāsyāmapāyāṃ vā kāryaṃ prātaḥ samāhitaiḥ //
2.42.d:
एतदेव विधानं तु मासि मासि च मोहिनि ।
पौर्णमास्यामपायां वा कार्यं प्रातः समाहितैः ॥
2.42.m: This very rite should be performed month after month, O Mohinī, / on the full-moon day or at its close, in the morning by the concentrated.

2.42.s:
varṣaṃ yastu naro bhaktyā yathā śaktyarcayanmudā /
haviṣyāśī mitāhāro brahmacaryasamanvitaḥ //
2.42.d:
वर्षं यस्तु नरो भक्त्या यथा शक्त्यर्चयन्मुदा ।
हविष्याशी मिताहारो ब्रह्मचर्यसमन्वितः ॥
2.42.m: Whatever man, joyfully worshiping for a year with devotion according to his means, / eating sacrificial food, eating moderately, observing chastity,

2.42.s:
dine vāpi tathā rātrā niyamena ca mohini /
saṃvatsarānte tasyeṣā gaṅgā divyavapurddharā //
2.42.d:
दिने वापि तथा रात्रा नियमेन च मोहिनि ।
संवत्सरान्ते तस्येषा गङ्गा दिव्यवपुर्द्धरा ॥
2.42.m: by day or by night under discipline, O Mohinī, / at the year's end, this Gaṅgā, assuming a divine form,

2.42.s:
divyamālyāṃbarā caiva divyaratnavibhūṣitā /
pratyakṣarūpā puratastiṣṭatyeva varapradā //
2.42.d:
दिव्यमाल्यांबरा चैव दिव्यरत्नविभूषिता ।
प्रत्यक्षरूपा पुरतस्तिष्टत्येव वरप्रदा ॥
2.42.m: adorned with divine garlands and garments, decked with divine jewels, / directly visible, stands before him, conferring boons.

2.42.s:
evaṃ pratyakṣarūpāṃ tāṃ gaṅgāṃ divyavapurddharām /
dṛṣṭvā sva cakṣuṣā martyaḥ kṛtakṛtyo bhavecchubhe //
2.42.d:
एवं प्रत्यक्षरूपां तां गङ्गां दिव्यवपुर्द्धराम् ।
दृष्ट्वा स्व चक्षुषा मर्त्यः कृतकृत्यो भवेच्छुभे ॥
2.42.m: Seeing thus with his own eyes that Gaṅgā directly visible, bearing a divine form, / a mortal becomes one who has achieved his goal, O auspicious woman.

2.42.s:
yānyānkāmayate martyaḥ kāmāṃstāṃstānavāpnuyāt /
niṣkāmastu labhenmokṣaṃ viprastenaiva janmanā //
2.42.d:
यान्यान्कामयते मर्त्यः कामांस्तांस्तानवाप्नुयात् ।
निष्कामस्तु लभेन्मोक्षं विप्रस्तेनैव जन्मना ॥
2.42.m: Whatever desires a mortal longs for, all those he obtains; / while one free from desires, even if a brāhmaṇa, attains liberation in that very birth.

2.42.s:
etaddhidhānaṃ ca mayoditaṃ te pṛṣṭaṃ hi sarvaṃ guḍadhenupūrvam /
gaṅgārcanaṃ muktikaraṃ vrataṃ tta sāṃvatsaraṃ śrīpatituṣṭidaṃ hi //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge mohinīvasusaṃvāde gaṅgāmāhātmye guḍadhenuvidhikathanaṃ nāma dvicatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.42.d:
एतद्धिधानं च मयोदितं ते पृष्टं हि सर्वं गुडधेनुपूर्वम् ।
गङ्गार्चनं मुक्तिकरं व्रतं त्त सांवत्सरं श्रीपतितुष्टिदं हि ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे मोहिनीवसुसंवादे गङ्गामाहात्म्ये गुडधेनुविधिकथनं नाम द्विचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
2.42.m:
Thus this rite has been declared by me to you, all that was asked, beginning with the jaggery-cow; / the year-long observance of worshiping the Gaṅgā brings liberation and delights the Lord of Śrī.

Thus ends the forty-second chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Rule for the Jaggery-Cow' in the eulogy of the greatness of the Gaṅgā, in the dialogue between Mohinī and Vasu, in the Uttarabubhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

2.43.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
vasorvacanamākarṇya gaṅgāmāhātmyasūcakam /
punaḥ papraccha rājendraṃ taṃ vipraṃ svapurohitam //
2.43.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
वसोर्वचनमाकर्ण्य गङ्गामाहात्म्यसूचकम् ।
पुनः पप्रच्छ राजेन्द्रं तं विप्रं स्वपुरोहितम् ॥
2.43.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Having heard Vasu's words revealing the greatness of the Gaṅgā, / O best of kings, she questioned that brāhmaṇa, her family priest, once again.

2.43.s:
mohinyuvāca
śrutaṃ vipra mayā sarvaṃ godānādi śubhāvaham /
adhunā śrotumicchāmi gaṅgāvratamanuttamam //
2.43.d:
मोहिन्युवाच
श्रुतं विप्र मया सर्वं गोदानादि शुभावहम् ।
अधुना श्रोतुमिच्छामि गङ्गाव्रतमनुत्तमम् ॥
2.43.m: Mohinī said: / O brāhmaṇa, all the auspicious rites such as the gift of cows have been heard by me; / now I wish to hear the peerless Gaṅgā observance.

2.43.s:
gaṅgādīnāṃ pūjanaṃ ca sthāpanaṃ tatra vā dvija /
kiṃ phalaṃ vada sarvajña tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatā //
2.43.d:
गङ्गादीनां पूजनं च स्थापनं तत्र वा द्विज ।
किं फलं वद सर्वज्ञ त्वामहं शरणं गता ॥
2.43.m: O twice-born, what is the reward for worshiping and establishing the Gaṅgā and others there? / Speak, O all-knowing one; I have taken refuge in you.

2.43.s:
adhunā gatidātā tvaṃ varjitāyāśca bandhubhiḥ /
patyā virahitā cāhaṃ putrahīnā vidāṃvara //
2.43.d:
अधुना गतिदाता त्वं वर्जितायाश्च बन्धुभिः ।
पत्या विरहिता चाहं पुत्रहीना विदांवर ॥
2.43.m: Now you are the giver of a refuge for me, who am abandoned by kin; / I am bereft of a husband and childless, O best of the wise.

2.43.s:
tvāmeva śaraṇaṃ prāptā piturvacanagauravāt /
tadbhavānpraṇatāyā me gaṅgāmāhātmyaṃsaṃyutam /
devatārādhanaṃ brūhi yacchrutvā mucyate hyaghāt //
2.43.d:
त्वामेव शरणं प्राप्ता पितुर्वचनगौरवात् ।
तद्भवान्प्रणताया मे गङ्गामाहात्म्यंसंयुतम् ।
देवताराधनं ब्रूहि यच्छ्रुत्वा मुच्यते ह्यघात् ॥
2.43.m: I have approached you alone for refuge out of respect for my father's word; / therefore, tell me, who am bowed down, of the worship of deities accompanied by the eulogy of the greatness of the Gaṅgā, hearing which one is freed from sin.

2.43.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
tacchrutvā mohinīvākyaṃ vasurvipraḥ pratāpavān /
sabhājya mohinīṃ bhūpa prāha vedavidāṃ varaḥ //
2.43.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
तच्छ्रुत्वा मोहिनीवाक्यं वसुर्विप्रः प्रतापवान् ।
सभाज्य मोहिनीं भूप प्राह वेदविदां वरः ॥
2.43.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Hearing those words of Mohinī, the glorious brāhmaṇa Vasu, / having honoured Mohinī, O king, spoke, the best among knowers of the Veda.

2.43.s:
vasuruvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā devi lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā //
2.43.d:
वसुरुवाच
साधु पृष्टं त्वया देवि लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
2.43.m: Vasu said: / Well asked by you, O lady, wishing the welfare of the worlds.

2.43.s:
gaṅgāmāhātmyamakhilaṃ mahāpāpapraṇāśanam /
vṛṣadhvajena kathitaṃ śivena dayayā purā //
2.43.d:
गङ्गामाहात्म्यमखिलं महापापप्रणाशनम् ।
वृषध्वजेन कथितं शिवेन दयया पुरा ॥
2.43.m: The entire eulogy of the greatness of the Gaṅgā, destroying great sins, / was previously spoken in mercy by Śiva, whose banner bears a bull,

2.43.s:
prītyā devyābhi pṛṣṭena gaṅgātīranivāsinā /
devaistu bhuktaṃ pūrvāhṇe madhyāhne ṛṣibhistathā //
2.43.d:
प्रीत्या देव्याभि पृष्टेन गङ्गातीरनिवासिना ।
देवैस्तु भुक्तं पूर्वाह्णे मध्याह्ने ऋषिभिस्तथा ॥
2.43.m: when affectionately asked by the goddess, [he who] dwells on the bank of the Gaṅgā. / Food is taken by the gods in the morning, and at noon by the sages;

2.43.s:
aparāhṇe ca pitṛbhiḥ śarvarṃyāṃ guhyakādibhaiḥ /
sarvā velā atikramya naktabhojanamuttamam //
2.43.d:
अपराह्णे च पितृभिः शर्वर्ंयां गुह्यकादिभैः ।
सर्वा वेला अतिक्रम्य नक्तभोजनमुत्तमम् ॥
2.43.m: in the afternoon by the ancestors, and at night by Guhyakas and the like. / Passing beyond all meal times, the evening meal is superior.

2.43.s:
upavāsādvāraṃ bhaikṣyaṃ bhaikṣyādvaramayācitam /
ayācitādvāraṃ naktaṃ tasmānnaktaṃ samācaret //
2.43.d:
उपवासाद्वारं भैक्ष्यं भैक्ष्याद्वरमयाचितम् ।
अयाचिताद्वारं नक्तं तस्मान्नक्तं समाचरेत् ॥
2.43.m: Better than fasting is alms-food; better than alms-food is unsolicited food; / better than unsolicited food is the evening meal; therefore one should observe the evening meal.

2.43.s:
haviṣyabhojanaṃ snānaṃ satyamāhāralāghavam /
agnikāryyamadhaḥśayyāṃ naktāśī ṣaṭ samācaret //
2.43.d:
हविष्यभोजनं स्नानं सत्यमाहारलाघवम् ।
अग्निकार्य्यमधःशय्यां नक्ताशी षट् समाचरेत् ॥
2.43.m: Eating sacrificial food, bathing, truthfulness, lightness of diet, / performing the fire rite, and sleeping on the ground—one who eats at night should practise these six.

2.43.s:
gaṅgātīre māghamāse yaḥ kuryānnaktabhojanam /
śivāyatanapārśve tu kṛśaraṃ ghṛtasaṃyutam //
2.43.d:
गङ्गातीरे माघमासे यः कुर्यान्नक्तभोजनम् ।
शिवायतनपार्श्वे तु कृशरं घृतसंयुतम् ॥
2.43.m: He who takes his evening meal on the bank of the Gaṅgā in the month of Māgha, / beside a shrine of Śiva, [eating] kṛśara mixed with ghee,

2.43.s:
naivedyaṃ ca nivedyaiva kṛśarānnaṃ śivasya tu /
kāṣṭhamaunena bhuñjāno jihvālaulyaṃ vivarjayet //
2.43.d:
नैवेद्यं च निवेद्यैव कृशरान्नं शिवस्य तु ।
काष्ठमौनेन भुञ्जानो जिह्वालौल्यं विवर्जयेत् ॥
2.43.m: and having offered that kṛśara rice as an oblation to Śiva, / eating in absolute silence, he should avoid greediness of the tongue.

2.43.s:
palāśapatre bhuñjānaḥ śivaṃ smṛtvā jitendriyaḥ /
dharmarājasya devyāśca pṛthakpiṇḍaṃ prakalpayet //
2.43.d:
पलाशपत्रे भुञ्जानः शिवं स्मृत्वा जितेन्द्रियः ।
धर्मराजस्य देव्याश्च पृथक्पिण्डं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
2.43.m: Eating from a palāśa leaf, remembering Śiva with senses controlled, / he should prepare a separate rice-ball for Dharmarāja and for the Goddess.

2.43.s:
sopavāsaścaturddaśyāṃ bhavedubhayapakṣayoḥ /
paurṇamāsyāṃ tu gandhaiśca gaṅgāyāḥ salilaistathā //
2.43.d:
सोपवासश्चतुर्द्दश्यां भवेदुभयपक्षयोः ।
पौर्णमास्यां तु गन्धैश्च गङ्गायाः सलिलैस्तथा ॥
2.43.m: He should fast on the fourteenth day in both fortnights; / and on the full-moon day, with perfumes and with the waters of the Gaṅgā,

2.43.s:
śivaṃ saṃsnāpya payasā madhvājyadadhibhiḥ pṛthak /
tathaiva hemapuṣpaṃ ca liṅgamūrdhni vinikṣipet //
2.43.d:
शिवं संस्नाप्य पयसा मध्वाज्यदधिभिः पृथक् ।
तथैव हेमपुष्पं च लिङ्गमूर्ध्नि विनिक्षिपेत् ॥
2.43.m: bathing Śiva separately with milk, honey, ghee, and curd, / he should likewise place a golden flower upon the top of the liṅga.

2.43.s:
tato dadyāttu śaktyaivāpūpañca ghṛtapācitam /
tilāḍhakaṃ pragṛhyātha śivaliṅgopari kṣipet //
2.43.d:
ततो दद्यात्तु शक्त्यैवापूपञ्च घृतपाचितम् ।
तिलाढकं प्रगृह्याथ शिवलिङ्गोपरि क्षिपेत् ॥
2.43.m: Then, according to one's capacity, one should offer a cake cooked in ghee; / and taking an āḍhaka of sesame seeds, one should cast them upon the Śiva-liṅga.

2.43.s:
nīlotpalaiśca sarveśaṃ pūjayetpaṅkajairapi /
tadalābhe tu sauvarṇaiḥ paṅkajaiḥ pūjayeddharam //
2.43.d:
नीलोत्पलैश्च सर्वेशं पूजयेत्पङ्कजैरपि ।
तदलाभे तु सौवर्णैः पङ्कजैः पूजयेद्धरम् ॥
2.43.m: One should worship the Lord of All with blue water-lilies and lotuses; / if they cannot be obtained, one should worship Hara with golden lotuses.

2.43.s:
pāyasaṃ cātra madhvaktaṃ ghṛtayuktaṃ ca guggulam /
ghṛtadīpaṃ tathā caiva candanādyairvilepanam //
2.43.d:
पायसं चात्र मध्वक्तं घृतयुक्तं च गुग्गुलम् ।
घृतदीपं तथा चैव चन्दनाद्यैर्विलेपनम् ॥
2.43.m: Here, milk-rice mixed with honey, guggulu accompanied by ghee, / a ghee lamp, and ointment with sandalwood and other perfumes,

2.43.s:
dadyādbhaktyā maheśāya tathā patraphalāni ca /
kṛṣṇagomithunaṃ caiva sarūpaṃ ca nivedayet //
2.43.d:
दद्याद्भक्त्या महेशाय तथा पत्रफलानि च ।
कृष्णगोमिथुनं चैव सरूपं च निवेदयेत् ॥
2.43.m: leaves and fruits should be offered with devotion to Maheśa; / and one should present a handsome pair of black cattle.

2.43.s:
bhojayedbrāhmaṇānaṣṭau māsāṃte tu sadakṣiṇān /
varjayenmadhu māṃsaṃ ca taṃ māsaṃ brahmacaryavān //
2.43.d:
भोजयेद्ब्राह्मणानष्टौ मासांते तु सदक्षिणान् ।
वर्जयेन्मधु मांसं च तं मासं ब्रह्मचर्यवान् ॥
2.43.m: At the end of the month, one should feed eight brāhmaṇas with fees; / and remaining celibate throughout that month, one should avoid honey and meat.

2.43.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā yathoddiṣṭamekavāramidaṃ vratam /
yamaiśca niyamairyuktaḥ śraddhābhaktiparāyaṇaḥ //
2.43.d:
एवं कृत्वा यथोद्दिष्टमेकवारमिदं व्रतम् ।
यमैश्च नियमैर्युक्तः श्रद्धाभक्तिपरायणः ॥
2.43.m: Having performed this vow even once as prescribed, / endowed with restraints and observances, intent on faith and devotion,

2.43.s:
iha bhogānavāpnoti pretya cānuttamāṃ gatim /
indranīlapratīkāśairvimānaiḥ śikhisaṃyuktaiḥ //
2.43.d:
इह भोगानवाप्नोति प्रेत्य चानुत्तमां गतिम् ।
इन्द्रनीलप्रतीकाशैर्विमानैः शिखिसंयुक्तैः ॥
2.43.m: one obtains enjoyments here and the unsurpassable goal after death; / in celestial chariots resembling sapphires and equipped with crests,

2.43.s:
divyaratnamayaiścaiva divyabhogasamanvitaiḥ /
gatvā śivapuraṃ ramyaṃ sarvasvakulasaṃyutaḥ //
2.43.d:
दिव्यरत्नमयैश्चैव दिव्यभोगसमन्वितैः ।
गत्वा शिवपुरं रम्यं सर्वस्वकुलसंयुतः ॥
2.43.m: made of divine gems and accompanied by celestial enjoyments, / having gone to the delightful city of Śiva together with one's entire family,

2.43.s:
suhṛdbhirvividhaiścaiva vividhānapyabhīpsitān /
bhuktvā bhogānaśeṣāṃśca yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam //
2.43.d:
सुहृद्भिर्विविधैश्चैव विविधानप्यभीप्सितान् ।
भुक्त्वा भोगानशेषांश्च यावदाभूतसंप्लवम् ॥
2.43.m: and with various friends, having tasted manifold desired / and endless enjoyments until the dissolution of all beings,

2.43.s:
tato bhavati dharmātmā jaṃbūdvīpapatistathā /
tatra bhuṅkte samastāṃśca bhogānvigatakalmaṣaḥ //
2.43.d:
ततो भवति धर्मात्मा जंबूद्वीपपतिस्तथा ।
तत्र भुङ्क्ते समस्तांश्च भोगान्विगतकल्मषः ॥
2.43.m: from there, righteous-minded, he becomes the lord of Jambūdvīpa; / there, free from taint, he enjoys all pleasures.

2.43.s:
surūpaḥ subhagaścaiva tathā vihitaśāsanaḥ /
sarvarogavinirmuktaḥ so 'pyetatphalabhāgbhavet //
2.43.d:
सुरूपः सुभगश्चैव तथा विहितशासनः ।
सर्वरोगविनिर्मुक्तः सो ऽप्येतत्फलभाग्भवेत् ॥
2.43.m: Handsome, fortunate, his commands obeyed, / and freed from all diseases, he too shares in this fruit.

2.43.s:
vaiśākhe śuklapakṣe vā caturdaśyāṃ samāhitaḥ /
śālyannaṃ kṣīrasaṃyuktaṃ yaḥ kuryānnaktabhojanam //
2.43.d:
वैशाखे शुक्लपक्षे वा चतुर्दश्यां समाहितः ।
शाल्यन्नं क्षीरसंयुक्तं यः कुर्यान्नक्तभोजनम् ॥
2.43.m: Or in the month of Vaiśākha, during the bright fortnight, composed on the fourteenth day, / whoever takes an evening meal consisting of cooked rice of winter paddy mixed with milk,

2.43.s:
śivaṃ saṃpūjya puṣpādyairbhojyaṃ tu saṃnivedya ca /
kāṣṭhamaunena bhuñjāno vaṭakāṣṭena vai tathā //
2.43.d:
शिवं संपूज्य पुष्पाद्यैर्भोज्यं तु संनिवेद्य च ।
काष्ठमौनेन भुञ्जानो वटकाष्टेन वै तथा ॥
2.43.m: having worshipped Śiva with flowers and other offerings, presenting the food, / eating while observing complete silence, using a twig of the banyan tree,

2.43.s:
maunena prayato bhūtvā kuryādvai dantadhāvanam /
śivaliṅgasamīpe tu gaṅgātīre niśi svapet //
2.43.d:
मौनेन प्रयतो भूत्वा कुर्याद्वै दन्तधावनम् ।
शिवलिङ्गसमीपे तु गङ्गातीरे निशि स्वपेत् ॥
2.43.m: purified, observing silence, should clean his teeth; / and at night he should sleep on the Gaṅgā riverbank near a Śiva-liṅga.

2.43.s:
paurṇamāsyāṃ prabhāte tu gaṅgāyāṃ vidhinā tathā /
snātvopavāsaṃ saṃkalpya kuryyājjāgaraṇaṃ niśi //
2.43.d:
पौर्णमास्यां प्रभाते तु गङ्गायां विधिना तथा ।
स्नात्वोपवासं संकल्प्य कुर्य्याज्जागरणं निशि ॥
2.43.m: In the morning of the full moon day, having bathed in the Gaṅgā / according to rule, resolving to fast, he should keep a vigil at night.

2.43.s:
liṅgaṃ ghṛtena saṃsnāpya puṣpagandhādibhistathā /
naivedyadhūpadīpaiśca saṃpūjya vṛṣabhaṃ śubham //
2.43.d:
लिङ्गं घृतेन संस्नाप्य पुष्पगन्धादिभिस्तथा ।
नैवेद्यधूपदीपैश्च संपूज्य वृषभं शुभम् ॥
2.43.m: Bathing the liṅga in ghee, and worshipping with flowers, perfumes, and so forth, / with food offerings, incense, and lamps, [and worshipping] an auspicious bull,

2.43.s:
suśvetapuṣpavastrādyairhāridraiścandanaistathā /
alaṅkṛtya vidhānena śivāya vinivedayet //
2.43.d:
सुश्वेतपुष्पवस्त्राद्यैर्हारिद्रैश्चन्दनैस्तथा ।
अलङ्कृत्य विधानेन शिवाय विनिवेदयेत् ॥
2.43.m: adorned in accordance with rule with pure white flowers, garments, / and turmeric-colored sandalwood, one should dedicate it to Śiva.

2.43.s:
brāhmaṇāṃśca yathāśakti pāyasena tu bhojayet /
evaṃ sakṛcca yo bhaktyā karoti śraddhayānvitaḥ //
2.43.d:
ब्राह्मणांश्च यथाशक्ति पायसेन तु भोजयेत् ।
एवं सकृच्च यो भक्त्या करोति श्रद्धयान्वितः ॥
2.43.m: And according to one's ability, one should feed brāhmaṇas with milk-rice; / whoever performs this even once with devotion and faith

2.43.s:
labhate daivapādonayugānāṃ dvisahasrakam /
tapaḥ kṛtvā tu niyamādyatpuṇyaṃ tadasaṃśayam //
2.43.d:
लभते दैवपादोनयुगानां द्विसहस्रकम् ।
तपः कृत्वा तु नियमाद्यत्पुण्यं तदसंशयम् ॥
2.43.m: obtains the merit that comes from practicing austerity under strict rules / for two thousand divine yugas less a quarter—of this there is no doubt.

2.43.s:
haṃsakundaprabhāyuktairvimānaiścandrasannibhaiḥ /
suśvetavṛṣayuktaiśca muktājālavibhūṣitaiḥ //
2.43.d:
हंसकुन्दप्रभायुक्तैर्विमानैश्चन्द्रसन्निभैः ।
सुश्वेतवृषयुक्तैश्च मुक्ताजालविभूषितैः ॥
2.43.m: In celestial chariots possessing the radiance of swans and kunda blossoms, resembling the moon, / yoked with pure white bulls and adorned with networks of pearls,

2.43.s:
svakīyapitṛbhiḥ sārddhaṃ prayātīśvaramandiram /
nīlotpalasuṃgandhābhiḥ surūpābhiḥ samantataḥ //
2.43.d:
स्वकीयपितृभिः सार्द्धं प्रयातीश्वरमन्दिरम् ।
नीलोत्पलसुंगन्धाभिः सुरूपाभिः समन्ततः ॥
2.43.m: he goes along with his own ancestors to the abode of the Lord; / with beloved women having all-around divine forms,

2.43.s:
kāntābhirdivyarūpābhirbhuktvā bhogānanekaśaḥ /
anantakālamaiśvaryayukto bhūtvā tato bhuvi //
2.43.d:
कान्ताभिर्दिव्यरूपाभिर्भुक्त्वा भोगाननेकशः ।
अनन्तकालमैश्वर्ययुक्तो भूत्वा ततो भुवि ॥
2.43.m: fragrant like blue lotuses, having enjoyed many pleasures, / and possessing sovereignty for an endless time, he is then on earth

2.43.s:
jāyate sa mahīpālaḥ kīrtyaiśvaryasamanvitaḥ /
ekacchatreṇa sa mahīṃ pālayatyājñayā saha //
2.43.d:
जायते स महीपालः कीर्त्यैश्वर्यसमन्वितः ।
एकच्छत्रेण स महीं पालयत्याज्ञया सह ॥
2.43.m: born as an earth-ruler endowed with fame and dominion; / under a single parasol, he protects the earth together with his royal command.

2.43.s:
ante vairāgyasaṃpanno gaṅgāṃ sa labhate punaḥ /
sa tayā śraddhayā yukto gaṅgāyāṃ maraṇaṃ labhet //
2.43.d:
अन्ते वैराग्यसंपन्नो गङ्गां स लभते पुनः ।
स तया श्रद्धया युक्तो गङ्गायां मरणं लभेत् ॥
2.43.m: At the end, endowed with dispassion, he attains the Gaṅgā again; / possessed of that faith, he attains death at the Gaṅgā.

2.43.s:
tathā tatra smṛtiṃ labdhvā mokṣamāpnoti sa dhruvam /
jyeṣṭhe māsi site pakṣe daśamyāṃ hastasaṃyute //
2.43.d:
तथा तत्र स्मृतिं लब्ध्वा मोक्षमाप्नोति स ध्रुवम् ।
ज्येष्ठे मासि सिते पक्षे दशम्यां हस्तसंयुते ॥
2.43.m: Regaining his memory there, he surely attains liberation. / In the month of Jyeṣṭha, in the bright fortnight, on the tenth day conjoined with the constellation Hasta,

2.43.s:
gaṅgātīre tu puruṣo nārī vā bhaktibhāvataḥ /
niśāyāṃ jāgaraṃ kṛtvā gaṅgāṃ daśavidhaistataḥ //
2.43.d:
गङ्गातीरे तु पुरुषो नारी वा भक्तिभावतः ।
निशायां जागरं कृत्वा गङ्गां दशविधैस्ततः ॥
2.43.m: on the Gaṅgā riverbank, a man or a woman, out of devotion, / keeping vigil at night, should then [worship] the Gaṅgā with tenfold

2.43.s:
puṣpairgandhaiśca naivedyaiḥ phalaiśca daśasaṃkhyāyā /
tathaiva dīpaistāṃbūlaiḥ pūjayecchraddhayānvitaḥ //
2.43.d:
पुष्पैर्गन्धैश्च नैवेद्यैः फलैश्च दशसंख्याया ।
तथैव दीपैस्तांबूलैः पूजयेच्छ्रद्धयान्वितः ॥
2.43.m: flowers, perfumes, food offerings, and fruits numbering ten, / and likewise with lamps and betel leaves, one should worship with faith.

2.43.s:
snātvā bhaktyā tu jāhnavyāṃ daśakṛtvo vidhānataḥ /
daśaprasṛti kṛṣṇaṃśca tilānsarpiśca vai jale //
2.43.d:
स्नात्वा भक्त्या तु जाह्नव्यां दशकृत्वो विधानतः ।
दशप्रसृति कृष्णंश्च तिलान्सर्पिश्च वै जले ॥
2.43.m: Having bathed with devotion in the Jāhnavī ten times according to rule, / one should offer ten handfuls of black sesame seeds and ghee into the water,

2.43.s:
saktupiṇḍānguḍapiṇḍāndadyācca daśasaṃkhyayā /
tato gaṅgātaṭe ramye hemnā rūpyeṇa vā tathā //
2.43.d:
सक्तुपिण्डान्गुडपिण्डान्दद्याच्च दशसंख्यया ।
ततो गङ्गातटे रम्ये हेम्ना रूप्येण वा तथा ॥
2.43.m: and ten balls of barley-flour and balls of jaggery; / then, on the delightful bank of the Gaṅgā, made of gold or silver,

2.43.s:
gaṅgāyāḥ pratimāṃ kṛtvā vakṣyamāṇasvarūpiṇīm /
padmasvastikacihnasya saṃsthitasya tathopari //
2.43.d:
गङ्गायाः प्रतिमां कृत्वा वक्ष्यमाणस्वरूपिणीम् ।
पद्मस्वस्तिकचिह्नस्य संस्थितस्य तथोपरि ॥
2.43.m: having fashioned an image of Gaṅgā having the form to be described, / placed upon a mark of a lotus and a svastika,

2.43.s:
vastrasragdāmakaṇṭhasya pūrṇakuṃbhasya copari /
saṃsthāpya pūjayeddevīṃ tadalābhe mṛdādi vā //
2.43.d:
वस्त्रस्रग्दामकण्ठस्य पूर्णकुंभस्य चोपरि ।
संस्थाप्य पूजयेद्देवीं तदलाभे मृदादि वा ॥
2.43.m: and having installed it atop a full jar whose neck is bound with a cloth and a garland, / one should worship the goddess; if unavailable, [one may use] clay and the like.

2.43.s:
atha tatrāpyaśaktaścellikhetpiṣṭena vai bhuvi /
caturbhujāṃ sunetrāṃ ca candrāyutasamaprabhām //
2.43.d:
अथ तत्राप्यशक्तश्चेल्लिखेत्पिष्टेन वै भुवि ।
चतुर्भुजां सुनेत्रां च चन्द्रायुतसमप्रभाम् ॥
2.43.m: Or if unable even in that, one should draw [her] on the ground with flour: / four-armed, fair-eyed, with radiance like ten thousand moons,

2.43.s:
cāmarairvījyamānāṃ ca śvetacchatropaśibhitām /
suprasannāṃ ca varadāṃ karuṇārdranijāntarām //
2.43.d:
चामरैर्वीज्यमानां च श्वेतच्छत्रोपशिभिताम् ।
सुप्रसन्नां च वरदां करुणार्द्रनिजान्तराम् ॥
2.43.m: fanned with chowries, adorned with a white parasol, / supremely gracious, boon-granting, her heart softened with compassion,

2.43.s:
sudhāplāvitabhūpṛṣṭhāṃ devādibhirabhiṣṭutām /
divyaratnaparītāṃ ca diṃvyamālyānulepanām //
2.43.d:
सुधाप्लावितभूपृष्ठां देवादिभिरभिष्टुताम् ।
दिव्यरत्नपरीतां च दिंव्यमाल्यानुलेपनाम् ॥
2.43.m: inundating the surface of the earth with nectar, praised by gods and others, / surrounded by divine gems, and wearing divine garlands and unguents.

2.43.s:
dhyātvā jale yathāproktāṃ tatrārcāyāṃ tu pūjayet /
vakṣyamāṇena mantreṇa kuryātpūjāṃ viśeṣataḥ //
2.43.d:
ध्यात्वा जले यथाप्रोक्तां तत्रार्चायां तु पूजयेत् ।
वक्ष्यमाणेन मन्त्रेण कुर्यात्पूजां विशेषतः ॥
2.43.m: Meditating upon her as described in the water, one should worship her there in the image; / one should perform the worship especially with the mantra that will be spoken.

2.43.s:
pañcāmṛtena ca snānamarcāyāṃ tu viśiṣyate /
pratimāgre sthaṇḍile tu gomayenopalepayet //
2.43.d:
पञ्चामृतेन च स्नानमर्चायां तु विशिष्यते ।
प्रतिमाग्रे स्थण्डिले तु गोमयेनोपलेपयेत् ॥
2.43.m: Bathing [the deity] in the image with the five nectars is especially commended; / on an altar before the image, one should smear [the ground] with cow dung.

2.43.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ maheśaṃ ca brahmāṇaṃ bhāskaraṃ tathā /
bhagīrathaṃ ca nṛpatiṃ himavantaṃ nageśvaram //
2.43.d:
नारायणं महेशं च ब्रह्माणं भास्करं तथा ।
भगीरथं च नृपतिं हिमवन्तं नगेश्वरम् ॥
2.43.m: Nārāyaṇa, Maheśa, Brahmā, and the sun, / King Bhagīratha, and Himavat, the lord of mountains,

2.43.s:
gandhapuṣpādibhiścaiva yathāśakti prapūjayet /
daśaprasthāṃ stilāndadyāddaśa viprebhya eva ca //
2.43.d:
गन्धपुष्पादिभिश्चैव यथाशक्ति प्रपूजयेत् ।
दशप्रस्थां स्तिलान्दद्याद्दश विप्रेभ्य एव च ॥
2.43.m: one should worship according to one's ability with perfumes, flowers, and the like; / and one should give ten prasthas of sesame seeds to ten brāhmaṇas.

2.43.s:
daśaprasthānyavāndadyāddaśa gavyairyathāhitān /
matsyakacchapamaṇḍūkamarādijalecarān //
2.43.d:
दशप्रस्थान्यवान्दद्याद्दश गव्यैर्यथाहितान् ।
मत्स्यकच्छपमण्डूकमरादिजलेचरान् ॥
2.43.m: One should give ten prasthas of barley, and ten [pots] properly prepared with cow-products; / aquatic creatures: fish, turtles, frogs, and marālas,

2.43.s:
kāritānvai yathāśakti svarṇena rajatena vā /
tadalābhe piṣṭamayānabhyarcya kusumādibhiḥ /
gaṅgāyāṃ prakṣipetpūrvvaṃ mantreṇaiva tu mantravit //
2.43.d:
कारितान्वै यथाशक्ति स्वर्णेन रजतेन वा ।
तदलाभे पिष्टमयानभ्यर्च्य कुसुमादिभिः ।
गङ्गायां प्रक्षिपेत्पूर्व्वं मन्त्रेणैव तु मन्त्रवित् ॥
2.43.m: fashioned according to ability out of gold or silver, / or if unavailable, made of flour, having worshipped them with flowers and so forth, / the knower of mantras should first cast into the Gaṅgā with the mantra.

2.43.s:
rathayātrādine tasminvibhave sati kārayet /
rathārūḍhapratikṛtiṃ gaṅgāyāstūttarāmukhām //
2.43.d:
रथयात्रादिने तस्मिन्विभवे सति कारयेत् ।
रथारूढप्रतिकृतिं गङ्गायास्तूत्तरामुखाम् ॥
2.43.m: On that chariot festival day, if wealth permits, one should cause to be made / an image of Gaṅgā mounted on a chariot, facing the north.

2.43.s:
bhramantyā darśanaṃ loke durlabhaṃ pāpakarmaṇām /
durgāyā rathayātrāsti tathaivātrāpi kārayet //
2.43.d:
भ्रमन्त्या दर्शनं लोके दुर्लभं पापकर्मणाम् ।
दुर्गाया रथयात्रास्ति तथैवात्रापि कारयेत् ॥
2.43.m: The sight of her circumambulating is difficult to obtain in the world for evildoers; / just as there is a chariot festival for Durgā, so should one make it here.

2.43.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā vidhānena vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ /
daśapāpairvakṣyamāṇaiḥ sadya eva vimucyate //
2.43.d:
एवं कृत्वा विधानेन वित्तशाठ्यविवर्जितः ।
दशपापैर्वक्ष्यमाणैः सद्य एव विमुच्यते ॥
2.43.m: Having done this according to rule, free from miserliness regarding wealth, / one is instantly liberated from the ten sins to be described:

2.43.s:
adattānāmupādānaṃ hiṃsā caivāvidhānataḥ /
paradāropasevā ca kāyikaṃ tribidhaṃ smṛtam //
2.43.d:
अदत्तानामुपादानं हिंसा चैवाविधानतः ।
परदारोपसेवा च कायिकं त्रिबिधं स्मृतम् ॥
2.43.m: taking what has not been given, unlawful violence, / and intercourse with another's wife are known as the three kinds of bodily sins.

2.43.s:
pāṃruṣyamanṛtaṃ vāpi paiśunyaṃ cāpi sarvaśaḥ /
asaṃbaddhapralāpaśca vācikaṃ syāccaturvidham //
2.43.d:
पांरुष्यमनृतं वापि पैशुन्यं चापि सर्वशः ।
असंबद्धप्रलापश्च वाचिकं स्याच्चतुर्विधम् ॥
2.43.m: Harshness, untruth, backbiting of all kinds, / and incoherent babble are the four kinds of vocal sins.

2.43.s:
paradravyeṣvabhidhyānaṃ manasāniṣṭacintanam /
vitathābhiniveśaśca mānasaṃ trividhaṃ smṛtam //
2.43.d:
परद्रव्येष्वभिध्यानं मनसानिष्टचिन्तनम् ।
वितथाभिनिवेशश्च मानसं त्रिविधं स्मृतम् ॥
2.43.m: Coveting another's goods, thinking of harm in the mind, / and adherence to falsehood are known as the three kinds of mental sins.

2.43.s:
etairdaśavidhaiḥ pāpaiḥ koṭijanmasamudbhavaiḥ /
mucyate nātra saṃdeho brahmaṇo vacanaṃ yathā //
2.43.d:
एतैर्दशविधैः पापैः कोटिजन्मसमुद्भवैः ।
मुच्यते नात्र संदेहो ब्रह्मणो वचनं यथा ॥
2.43.m: From these ten kinds of sins originating in ten million births / one is freed, there is no doubt in this, just as Brahmā's word declares.

2.43.s:
daśa triṃśacca tānpūrvānpitṝneva tathāparān /
uddharatyeva saṃsārānmantreṇānena pūjitā //
2.43.d:
दश त्रिंशच्च तान्पूर्वान्पितॄनेव तथापरान् ।
उद्धरत्येव संसारान्मन्त्रेणानेन पूजिता ॥
2.43.m:
Worshipped with this mantra, she certainly delivers from saṃsāra
ten and thirty of those preceding ancestors, and likewise subsequent ones.

2.43.s:
oṃ namo daśaharāyai nārāyaṇyai gaṅgāyai namaḥ /
iti mantreṇa yo martyo dine tasmindivāniśam //
2.43.d:
ओं नमो दशहरायै नारायण्यै गङ्गायै नमः ।
इति मन्त्रेण यो मर्त्यो दिने तस्मिन्दिवानिशम् ॥
2.43.m:
"Oṃ, homage to Daśaharā, homage to Nārāyaṇī, to Gaṅgā."
With this mantra, whichever mortal, day and night on that day,

2.43.s:
japetpacasahasrāṇi daśadharmaphalaṃ labhet /
uddareddaśa pūrvāṇi parāṇi ca bhavārṇavāt //
2.43.d:
जपेत्पचसहस्राणि दशधर्मफलं लभेत् ।
उद्दरेद्दश पूर्वाणि पराणि च भवार्णवात् ॥
2.43.m:
recites five thousand [times], obtains the fruit of ten merits,
and rescues ten preceding and subsequent [ancestors] from the ocean of worldly existence.

2.43.s:
vakṣyamāṇamidaṃ stotraṃ vidhinā pratigṛhya ca /
gaṅgāgre taddine japyaṃ viṣṇupūjāṃ pravartayet //
2.43.d:
वक्ष्यमाणमिदं स्तोत्रं विधिना प्रतिगृह्य च ।
गङ्गाग्रे तद्दिने जप्यं विष्णुपूजां प्रवर्तयेत् ॥
2.43.m:
Having duly received this praise which will be spoken,
one should recite it before Gaṅgā on that day, and perform Viṣṇu's worship:

2.43.s:
oṃ namaḥ śivāyai gaṅgāyai śivadāyai namo 'stu te /
namo 'stu viṣṇurūpiṇyai gaṅgāyai te namo namaḥ //
2.43.d:
ओं नमः शिवायै गङ्गायै शिवदायै नमो ऽस्तु ते ।
नमो ऽस्तु विष्णुरूपिण्यै गङ्गायै ते नमो नमः ॥
2.43.m:
"Oṃ, homage to Śivā, to Gaṅgā, the giver of auspiciousness, homage be to you!
Homage be to the embodiment of Viṣṇu, homage, homage to you, Gaṅgā!

2.43.s:
sarvadevasvarūpiṇyai namo bheṣajamūrtaye /
sarvasya sarvavyādhīnāṃ bhiṣakśreṣṭhe namo 'stu te //
2.43.d:
सर्वदेवस्वरूपिण्यै नमो भेषजमूर्तये ।
सर्वस्य सर्वव्याधीनां भिषक्श्रेष्ठे नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
2.43.m:
Homage to the embodiment of all gods, whose form is medicine;
homage be to you, the best of physicians for all diseases of everyone!

2.43.s:
sthāṇujaṅgamasaṃbhūtaviṣahantri namo 'stu te /
saṃsāraviṣanāśinyai jīvanāyai namonamaḥ //
2.43.d:
स्थाणुजङ्गमसंभूतविषहन्त्रि नमो ऽस्तु ते ।
संसारविषनाशिन्यै जीवनायै नमोनमः ॥
2.43.m:
O destroyer of poison arising from immovable and moving creatures, homage be to you!
Homage, homage to the destroyer of the poison of saṃsāra, the life-giver!

2.43.s:
tāpatritayahantryai ca prāṇeśvaryai namonamaḥ /
śāntyai saṃtāpahāriṇyai namaste sarvamūrtaye //
2.43.d:
तापत्रितयहन्त्र्यै च प्राणेश्वर्यै नमोनमः ।
शान्त्यै संतापहारिण्यै नमस्ते सर्वमूर्तये ॥
2.43.m:
Homage, homage to the destroyer of the three afflictions, the mistress of life!
Homage to you, peace, the remover of torment, whose form is everything!

2.43.s:
sarvasaṃśuddhikāriṇyai namaḥ pāpavimuktaye /
bhuktimuktipradāyinyai bhogavatyai namonamaḥ //
2.43.d:
सर्वसंशुद्धिकारिण्यै नमः पापविमुक्तये ।
भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायिन्यै भोगवत्यै नमोनमः ॥
2.43.m:
Homage to the cause of complete purification, for the release from sin!
Homage, homage to the bestower of enjoyment and liberation, to Bhogavatī!

2.43.s:
mandākinyai namaste 'stu svargadāyai namonamaḥ /
namastrailokyamūrtāyai tridaśāyai namonamaḥ //
2.43.d:
मन्दाकिन्यै नमस्ते ऽस्तु स्वर्गदायै नमोनमः ।
नमस्त्रैलोक्यमूर्तायै त्रिदशायै नमोनमः ॥
2.43.m:
Homage be to you, Mandākinī, bestower of heaven, homage, homage!
Homage, homage to the embodiment of the three worlds, to the deity!

2.43.s:
namaste śuklasaṃsthāyai kṣemavatyai namonamaḥ /
tridaśāsanasaṃsthāyai tejovatyai namo 'stu te //
2.43.d:
नमस्ते शुक्लसंस्थायै क्षेमवत्यै नमोनमः ।
त्रिदशासनसंस्थायै तेजोवत्यै नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
2.43.m:
Homage to you who abide in purity, homage, homage to Kṣemavatī!
Homage be to you who reside on the throne of the gods, full of splendor!

2.43.s:
mandāyai liṅgadhāriṇyai nārāyaṇyai namonamaḥ /
namaste viśvamitrāyai revatyai te namonamaḥ //
2.43.d:
मन्दायै लिङ्गधारिण्यै नारायण्यै नमोनमः ।
नमस्ते विश्वमित्रायै रेवत्यै ते नमोनमः ॥
2.43.m:
Homage, homage to Mandā, the bearer of the liṅga, to Nārāyaṇī!
Homage to you, friend of the universe, homage, homage to you, Revatī!

2.43.s:
bṛhatyai te namo nityaṃ lokadhātryai namonamaḥ /
namaste viśvamukhyāyai nandinyai te namonamaḥ //
2.43.d:
बृहत्यै ते नमो नित्यं लोकधात्र्यै नमोनमः ।
नमस्ते विश्वमुख्यायै नन्दिन्यै ते नमोनमः ॥
2.43.m:
Homage always to you, the immense, homage, homage to the sustainer of the world!
Homage to you, foremost of the universe, homage, homage to you, Nandinī!

2.43.s:
pṛthvyai śivāmṛtāyai ca virajāyai namonamaḥ /
parāvaragatādyaiyai tārāyai te namonamaḥ //
2.43.d:
पृथ्व्यै शिवामृतायै च विरजायै नमोनमः ।
परावरगताद्यैयै तारायै ते नमोनमः ॥
2.43.m:
Homage, homage to the earth, the nectar of Śiva, the passionless one!
Homage, homage to you, the primordial one moving through high and low, the savior!

2.43.s:
namaste svargasaṃsthāyai abhinnāyai namonamaḥ /
śāntāyai te pratiṣṭhāyai varadāyai namonamaḥ //
2.43.d:
नमस्ते स्वर्गसंस्थायै अभिन्नायै नमोनमः ।
शान्तायै ते प्रतिष्ठायै वरदायै नमोनमः ॥
2.43.m:
Homage to you who abide in heaven, homage, homage to the undivided!
Homage, homage to you, tranquil, the foundation, the giver of boons!

2.43.s:
ugrāyai nukhajalpāyai saṃjīvinyai namonamaḥ /
brahmagāyai brahmadāyai duritaghnyai namonamaḥ //
2.43.d:
उग्रायै नुखजल्पायै संजीविन्यै नमोनमः ।
ब्रह्मगायै ब्रह्मदायै दुरितघ्न्यै नमोनमः ॥
2.43.m:
Homage, homage to the fierce one, resonant with speech, the reviver!
Homage, homage to the one who leads to Brahman, the giver of Brahman, the destroyer of sin!

2.43.s:
praṇatārtiprabhañjinyai jaganmātre namonamaḥ /
viluṣāyai durgahantryai dakṣāyai te namonamaḥ //
2.43.d:
प्रणतार्तिप्रभञ्जिन्यै जगन्मात्रे नमोनमः ।
विलुषायै दुर्गहन्त्र्यै दक्षायै ते नमोनमः ॥
2.43.m:
Homage, homage to the shatterer of the distress of the bowed, to the Mother of the world!
Homage, homage to you, the consumer of sins, destroyer of misfortune, capable one!

2.43.s:
sarvāpatpratipakṣāyai maṅgalāyai namonamaḥ /
parāpare pare tubhya namo mokṣaprade sadā /
gaṅgā mamāgrato bhūyādgaṅgā me pārśvayostathā //
2.43.d:
सर्वापत्प्रतिपक्षायै मङ्गलायै नमोनमः ।
परापरे परे तुभ्य नमो मोक्षप्रदे सदा ।
गङ्गा ममाग्रतो भूयाद्गङ्गा मे पार्श्वयोस्तथा ॥

2.43.s:
gaṅgā me sarvato bhūyāttvayi gaṅge 'stu me sthitiḥ /
ādau tvamante madhye ca sarvā tvaṃ gāṅgate śive //
2.43.d:
गङ्गा मे सर्वतो भूयात्त्वयि गङ्गे ऽस्तु मे स्थितिः ।
आदौ त्वमन्ते मध्ये च सर्वा त्वं गाङ्गते शिवे ॥
2.43.m:
may Gaṅgā be on all sides of me; may my abiding be in you, O Gaṅgā!
At the beginning, at the end, and in the middle, you are everything, O Gaṅgā, O auspicious one!

2.43.s:
tvameva mūlaprakṛtistvaṃ hi nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ /
gaṅge tvaṃ paramātmā ca śivastubhyaṃ namonamaḥ //
2.43.d:
त्वमेव मूलप्रकृतिस्त्वं हि नारायणः प्रभुः ।
गङ्गे त्वं परमात्मा च शिवस्तुभ्यं नमोनमः ॥
2.43.m:
You alone are primordial nature; you indeed are Nārāyaṇa, the Lord.
O Gaṅgā, you are the Supreme Self and Śiva. Homage, homage to you!"

2.43.s:
itīdaṃ paṭhati stotraṃ nityaṃ bhaktiparastu yaḥ /
śṛṇoti śraddhayā vāpi kāyavācikasaṃbhavaiḥ //
2.43.d:
इतीदं पठति स्तोत्रं नित्यं भक्तिपरस्तु यः ।
शृणोति श्रद्धया वापि कायवाचिकसंभवैः ॥
2.43.m:
He who, devoted, recites this praise daily,
or even hears it with faith, arising from body and speech,

2.43.s:
daśadhā saṃsthitairdeṣaiḥ sarvaireva pramucyate /
rogī pramucyate rogānmucyetāpanna āpadaḥ //
2.43.d:
दशधा संस्थितैर्देषैः सर्वैरेव प्रमुच्यते ।
रोगी प्रमुच्यते रोगान्मुच्येतापन्न आपदः ॥
2.43.m:
is freed from all faults existing in ten ways.
The sick is freed from sickness, the afflicted would be freed from calamity;

2.43.s:
dviṣabhdyo bandhanāccāpi bhayebhyaśca vimucyate /
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti pretya brahmaṇi līyate //
2.43.d:
द्विषभ्द्यो बन्धनाच्चापि भयेभ्यश्च विमुच्यते ।
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति प्रेत्य ब्रह्मणि लीयते ॥
2.43.m:
he is freed also from enemies, from bondages, and from fears;
he attains all desires, and after dying merges into Brahman.

2.43.s:
idaṃ stotraṃ gṛhe yasya likhitaṃ paripūjyate /
nāgnicaurabhayaṃ tatra pāpebhyo 'pi bhayaṃ nahi //
2.43.d:
इदं स्तोत्रं गृहे यस्य लिखितं परिपूज्यते ।
नाग्निचौरभयं तत्र पापेभ्यो ऽपि भयं नहि ॥
2.43.m:
In whose house this hymn is written and worshipped,
there is no danger from fire or thieves, nor any fear from sins.

2.43.s:
tasyāṃ daśamyāmetacca stotraṃ gaṅgājale sthitaḥ /
japaṃstu daśakṛtvaśca daridro vāpi cākṣamaḥ //
2.43.d:
तस्यां दशम्यामेतच्च स्तोत्रं गङ्गाजले स्थितः ।
जपंस्तु दशकृत्वश्च दरिद्रो वापि चाक्षमः ॥
2.43.m:
Standing in the waters of Gaṅgā on that tenth day,
reciting this hymn ten times, even a poor or disabled person,

2.43.s:
so 'pi tatphalamāpnoti gaṅgāṃ saṃpūjya bhaktitaḥ /
pūrvoktena vidhānena phalaṃ yatparikīrtitam //
2.43.d:
सो ऽपि तत्फलमाप्नोति गङ्गां संपूज्य भक्तितः ।
पूर्वोक्तेन विधानेन फलं यत्परिकीर्तितम् ॥
2.43.m:
he too attains that fruit, having worshipped Gaṅgā with devotion
according to the previously stated rite—the fruit which has been proclaimed.

2.43.s:
yathā gaurī tathā gaṅgā tasmādgauryāstu pūjane /
vidhiryo vihitaḥ samyakso 'pi gaṅgāprapūjane //
2.43.d:
यथा गौरी तथा गङ्गा तस्माद्गौर्यास्तु पूजने ।
विधिर्यो विहितः सम्यक्सो ऽपि गङ्गाप्रपूजने ॥
2.43.m:
As is Gaurī, so is Gaṅgā; therefore in the worship of Gaurī
whatever rite is duly prescribed, that same applies in the thorough worship of Gaṅgā.

2.43.s:
yathā śivastathā viṣṇuryathā viṣṇustathā hyumā /
umā yathā tathā gaṅgā cātra bhedo na vidyate //
2.43.d:
यथा शिवस्तथा विष्णुर्यथा विष्णुस्तथा ह्युमा ।
उमा यथा तथा गङ्गा चात्र भेदो न विद्यते ॥
2.43.m:
As is Śiva, so is Viṣṇu; as is Viṣṇu, so indeed is Umā;
as is Umā, so is Gaṅgā; no difference is found here.

2.43.s:
viṣṇurudrāntaraṃ yaśca gagāgauryantaraṃ tathā /
lakṣmīgauryataraṃ yaśca prabrūte mūḍhadhīstu saḥ //
2.43.d:
विष्णुरुद्रान्तरं यश्च गगागौर्यन्तरं तथा ।
लक्ष्मीगौर्यतरं यश्च प्रब्रूते मूढधीस्तु सः ॥
2.43.m:
Whoever speaks of a difference between Viṣṇu and Rudra, and likewise between Gaṅgā and Gaurī,
and whoever speaks of a difference between Lakṣmī and Gaurī, that person is foolish-minded.

2.43.s:
śuklapakṣe divā bhūmau gaṅgāyāmuttarāyaṇe /
dhanyā dehaṃ vimuñcanti hṛdayasthe janārdane //
2.43.d:
शुक्लपक्षे दिवा भूमौ गङ्गायामुत्तरायणे ।
धन्या देहं विमुञ्चन्ति हृदयस्थे जनार्दने ॥
2.43.m:
In the bright fortnight, by day, on the earth, in the Gaṅgā, during the northern solstice,
the blessed shed the body with Janārdana situated in their heart.

2.43.s:
ye muñcanti narā-prāṇān gaṅgāyāṃ vidhinaṃ dini /
te viṣṇulokaṃ gacchanti stūyamānā divisthitaiḥ //
2.43.d:
ये मुञ्चन्ति नरा-प्राणान् गङ्गायां विधिनं दिनि ।
ते विष्णुलोकं गच्छन्ति स्तूयमाना दिविस्थितैः ॥
2.43.m:
Men who surrender their life-breaths in the Gaṅgā on an auspicious day,
go to the world of Viṣṇu, praised by those dwelling in heaven.

2.43.s:
arddhodakena jāhnavyāṃ mniyate 'naśanena yaḥ /
sa yāti na punarjanma brahmasāyujyameti ca //
2.43.d:
अर्द्धोदकेन जाह्नव्यां म्नियते ऽनशनेन यः ।
स याति न पुनर्जन्म ब्रह्मसायुज्यमेति च ॥
2.43.m:
He who dies in the Jāhnavī half-immersed in water, by fasting,
goes to no rebirth and attains union with Brahman.

2.43.s:
yā gatiryogayuktasya sātvikasya manīṣiṇaḥ /
sā getistyajataḥ prāṇān gaṅgāyāṃ tu śarīriṇaḥ //
2.43.d:
या गतिर्योगयुक्तस्य सात्विकस्य मनीषिणः ।
सा गेतिस्त्यजतः प्राणान् गङ्गायां तु शरीरिणः ॥
2.43.m:
Whatever destination belongs to the wise person of pure sattva engaged in yoga,
that same destination belongs to the embodied soul relinquishing life-breaths in the Gaṅgā.

2.43.s:
anaśanaṃ gṛhītvā yo gaṅgātīre mṛto naraḥ /
satyameva paraṃ lokamāpnoti pitṛbhiḥ saha //
2.43.d:
अनशनं गृहीत्वा यो गङ्गातीरे मृतो नरः ।
सत्यमेव परं लोकमाप्नोति पितृभिः सह ॥
2.43.m:
A man who dies on the riverbank of the Gaṅgā having undertaken fasting,
truly reaches the supreme world together with his ancestors.

2.43.s:
gaṅgāyāṃ maraṇātprāṇānyoḥ prājñastyaktumicchati /
gatāni bahujanmāni yatra yatra mṛtāni ca //
2.43.d:
गङ्गायां मरणात्प्राणान्योः प्राज्ञस्त्यक्तुमिच्छति ।
गतानि बहुजन्मानि यत्र यत्र मृतानि च ॥
2.43.m:
When a wise man wishes to relinquish his life-breaths through death in the Gaṅgā,
many past births wherever they may have perished,

2.43.s:
mahāṃścāpi gataḥ kālo yatra tatrāpi gacchataḥ /
atradūre samīpe ca sadṛśaṃ yojanadvayam //
2.43.d:
महांश्चापि गतः कालो यत्र तत्रापि गच्छतः ।
अत्रदूरे समीपे च सदृशं योजनद्वयम् ॥
2.43.m:
and also a vast time has passed wherever he may go;
here, whether far or near, a distance of two yojanas is equal.

2.43.s:
gaṅgāyāṃ maraṇeneha nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
jñānato 'jñānato vāpi kāmato 'pi vā //
2.43.d:
गङ्गायां मरणेनेह नात्र कार्या विचारणा ।
ज्ञानतो ऽज्ञानतो वापि कामतो ऽपि वा ॥
2.43.m:
By death in the Gaṅgā here, no hesitation should be made in this regard,
whether [done] consciously or unconsciously, or even intentionally.

2.43.s:
gaṅgāyāṃ tu mṛto martyaḥ svargaṃ mokṣaṃ ca vindati /
prāṇeṣūtsṛjyamāneṣu yo gaṅgāṃ saṃsmarennaraḥ //
2.43.d:
गङ्गायां तु मृतो मर्त्यः स्वर्गं मोक्षं च विन्दति ।
प्राणेषूत्सृज्यमानेषु यो गङ्गां संस्मरेन्नरः ॥
2.43.m:
A mortal dead in the Gaṅgā attains heaven and liberation.
A person who remembers Gaṅgā when life-breaths are being relinquished,

2.43.s: spṛśedvā pāpaśīlo 'pi sa vai yāti parāṃ gatim //
2.43.d: स्पृशेद्वा पापशीलो ऽपि स वै याति परां गतिम् ॥
2.43.m: or touches [her], even if of sinful conduct, goes indeed to the supreme destination.

2.43.s:
gaṅgāṃ gatvā yaiḥ śarīraṃ visṛṣṭaṃ prāptā dhīrāste tu devaiḥ samatvam /
tasmātsurvānprohya muktipradānvai sevedgaṅgāmā śarīrasya pātam //
2.43.d:
गङ्गां गत्वा यैः शरीरं विसृष्टं प्राप्ता धीरास्ते तु देवैः समत्वम् ।
तस्मात्सुर्वान्प्रोह्य मुक्तिप्रदान्वै सेवेद्गङ्गामा शरीरस्य पातम् ॥
2.43.m:
Those steadfast ones who have abandoned their body having gone to Gaṅgā have attained equality with the gods;
therefore, leaving aside all else, one should certainly serve Gaṅgā, which bestows liberation, until the fall of the body.

2.43.s:
antarikṣe kṣitau toye pāpīyānapi yo mṛtaḥ /
brahmaviṣṇuśivaiḥ pūjyaṃ padamakṣayyamaśnute //
2.43.d:
अन्तरिक्षे क्षितौ तोये पापीयानपि यो मृतः ।
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवैः पूज्यं पदमक्षय्यमश्नुते ॥
2.43.m:
Even a very sinful person who has died in the intermediate space, on the earth, or in water,
enjoys an imperishable state worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.

2.43.s:
yo dharmiśṭaśca saprāṇaḥ prayataḥ śiṣṭasaṃmataḥ /
cintayenmanasā gaṅgāṃ sa gatiṃ paramāṃ labhet //
2.43.d:
यो धर्मिश्टश्च सप्राणः प्रयतः शिष्टसंमतः ।
चिन्तयेन्मनसा गङ्गां स गतिं परमां लभेत् ॥
2.43.m:
One who is very righteous, with life-breath intact, restrained, approved by the virtuous,
should contemplate Gaṅgā with his mind; he shall obtain the supreme destination.

2.43.s:
yatra tatra mṛto vāpi maraṇe samupasthite /
bhaktyā gaṅgāṃ smaranyāti śaivaṃ vā vaiṣṇavaṃ puram //
2.43.d:
यत्र तत्र मृतो वापि मरणे समुपस्थिते ।
भक्त्या गङ्गां स्मरन्याति शैवं वा वैष्णवं पुरम् ॥
2.43.m:
Dead anywhere, when death is at hand,
remembering Gaṅgā with devotion, one goes to the realm of Śiva or Viṣṇu.

2.43.s:
śaṃbhorjaṭākalāpāttu viniṣkrāntātikarkaśāt /
plāvayitvā divaṃ ninye yā pāpānyagarātmajān //
2.43.d:
शंभोर्जटाकलापात्तु विनिष्क्रान्तातिकर्कशात् ।
प्लावयित्वा दिवं निन्ये या पापान्यगरात्मजान् ॥
2.43.m:
Emerging from Śambhu's matted hair, exceedingly rugged,
she who, having inundated them, led the sinful sons of Sagara to heaven.

2.43.s:
yāvantyasthīni gaṅgāyāṃ tiṣṭhanti puruṣasya vai /
