tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate //
2.43.d:
यावन्त्यस्थीनि गङ्गायां तिष्ठन्ति पुरुषस्य वै ।
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
2.43.m:
For as many thousands of years as the bones of a person
remain in the Gaṅgā, he is honored in the heavenly world.

2.43.s:
gagātoye tu yasyāsthi nītvā prakṣipyate naraiḥ /
tatkālamāditaḥ kṛtvā svargaloke bhavetsthitiḥ //
2.43.d:
गगातोये तु यस्यास्थि नीत्वा प्रक्षिप्यते नरैः ।
तत्कालमादितः कृत्वा स्वर्गलोके भवेत्स्थितिः ॥
2.43.m:
In the water of the Gaṅgā, whose bone is carried and cast by men,
reckoning from that very moment, his residence is in the heavenly world.

2.43.s:
gaṅgātoye tu yasyāsthi prāpyate śubhakarmaṇaḥ /
na tasya punarāvṛttirbrahmalokātkathañcana //
2.43.d:
गङ्गातोये तु यस्यास्थि प्राप्यते शुभकर्मणः ।
न तस्य पुनरावृत्तिर्ब्रह्मलोकात्कथञ्चन ॥
2.43.m:
Whose bone of meritorious deed is placed in the water of Gaṅgā,
for him there is no return from the world of Brahmā by any means.

2.43.s:
daśāhābhyantare yasya gaṅgātoye 'sthi saṃgatam /
gaṅgāyāṃ maraṇe yādṛktādṛkphalamavāpnuyāt //
2.43.d:
दशाहाभ्यन्तरे यस्य गङ्गातोये ऽस्थि संगतम् ।
गङ्गायां मरणे यादृक्तादृक्फलमवाप्नुयात् ॥
2.43.m: If a person's bones enter the water of the Gaṅgā within ten days, / he attains the same fruit as that of dying in the Gaṅgā.

2.43.s:
snātvā tataḥ pañcagavyena siktvā hiraṇyamadhvājyatilairniyojya /
tadasthipiṇḍaṃ puṭake nidhāya paśyan diśaṃ pretagaṇopagūḍhām //
2.43.d:
स्नात्वा ततः पञ्चगव्येन सिक्त्वा हिरण्यमध्वाज्यतिलैर्नियोज्य ।
तदस्थिपिण्डं पुटके निधाय पश्यन् दिशं प्रेतगणोपगूढाम् ॥
2.43.m: Having bathed, sprinkled [them] with the five products of the cow, joined [them] with gold, honey, clarified butter, and sesame seeds, / placed that bone-piṇḍa inside a leaf-cup, looking toward the direction occupied by the hosts of the dead,

2.43.s:
namo 'stu dharmāya vadanpraviśya jalaṃ sa me prīta iti kṣipecca /
snātvā tatastīrthavaṭākṣayaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā pradadyādatha dakṣiṇāṃ tu //
2.43.d:
नमो ऽस्तु धर्माय वदन्प्रविश्य जलं स मे प्रीत इति क्षिपेच्च ।
स्नात्वा ततस्तीर्थवटाक्षयं च दृष्ट्वा प्रदद्यादथ दक्षिणां तु ॥
2.43.m: saying 'Obeisance be to Dharma,' entering the water, saying 'May he be pleased with me,' he should cast [it in]. / Then, having bathed and viewed the imperishable banyan of the sacred ford, he should indeed offer a priestly gift.

2.43.s: evaṃ kṛtvā pretapure sthitasya svarge gatiḥ syātta mahendratulyā //
2.43.d: एवं कृत्वा प्रेतपुरे स्थितस्य स्वर्गे गतिः स्यात्त महेन्द्रतुल्या ॥
2.43.m: Having acted thus, the one dwelling in the city of the dead shall have a course in heaven equal to that of great Indra.

2.43.s:
pravāhamavadhiṃ kṛtvā yāvaddhastacatuṣṭayam /
tatra nārāyaṇaḥ svāmī nānyaḥ svāmī kadācana //
2.43.d:
प्रवाहमवधिं कृत्वा यावद्धस्तचतुष्टयम् ।
तत्र नारायणः स्वामी नान्यः स्वामी कदाचन ॥
2.43.m: Taking the current as the boundary, as far as four cubits, / there Nārāyaṇa is the owner; no one else is ever the owner.

2.43.s:
na tatra pratigṛhṇīyātprāṇaiḥ kaṇṭhagatairapi /
bhādraśuklacaturdaśyāṃ yāvadākramate jalam //
2.43.d:
न तत्र प्रतिगृह्णीयात्प्राणैः कण्ठगतैरपि ।
भाद्रशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां यावदाक्रमते जलम् ॥
2.43.m: One should make no acceptance of gifts there, even if one's life-breaths have reached the throat. / As far as the water reaches on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Bhādrapada,

2.43.s:
tāvadgabhaṃ vijānīyāttaddūraṃ tīramucyate /
sārddhahastaśataṃ yāvadgarbhastīraṃ tataḥ param //
2.43.d:
तावद्गभं विजानीयात्तद्दूरं तीरमुच्यते ।
सार्द्धहस्तशतं यावद्गर्भस्तीरं ततः परम् ॥
2.43.m: that much should be known as the riverbed; beyond that, it is called the riverbank. / As far as one hundred and fifty cubits is the riverbed; beyond that is the riverbank.

2.43.s:
iti keṣāṃ mataṃ devi śrutismṛtiṣu saṃmatam /
tīrādgavyūtimātraṃ tu paritaḥ kṣetramucyate //
2.43.d:
इति केषां मतं देवि श्रुतिस्मृतिषु संमतम् ।
तीराद्गव्यूतिमात्रं तु परितः क्षेत्रमुच्यते ॥
2.43.m: Such is the opinion of some, O goddess, agreed upon in the Vedas and traditions. / But all around, up to one gavyūti from the riverbank, it is called the sacred field.

2.43.s:
tīraṃ tyaktvā vasetkṣetre tīre vāso na ceṣyate /
ekayojanavistīrṇā kṣetrasīmā taṭadvayāt //
2.43.d:
तीरं त्यक्त्वा वसेत्क्षेत्रे तीरे वासो न चेष्यते ।
एकयोजनविस्तीर्णा क्षेत्रसीमा तटद्वयात् ॥
2.43.m: Leaving the riverbank, one should live in the sacred field; dwelling on the riverbank is not desired. / The boundary of the sacred field extends one yojana from both banks.

2.43.s:
gaṅgāsīmāṃ na laghanti pāpānyapyakhilānyapi /
tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā palāyante yathā siṃhaṃ vanaukasaḥ //
2.43.d:
गङ्गासीमां न लघन्ति पापान्यप्यखिलान्यपि ।
तां तु दृष्ट्वा पलायन्ते यथा सिंहं वनौकसः ॥
2.43.m: Even all sins do not cross the boundary of the Gaṅgā; / seeing it, they flee, just as forest-dwellers flee from a lion.

2.43.s:
yatra gaṅgā mahābhāge rāmaśaṃbhutapovanam /
siddhakṣetraṃ tu tajjñeyaṃ samantāttu triyojanam //
2.43.d:
यत्र गङ्गा महाभागे रामशंभुतपोवनम् ।
सिद्धक्षेत्रं तु तज्ज्ञेयं समन्तात्तु त्रियोजनम् ॥
2.43.m: O fortunate one, where the Gaṅgā is the penance-grove of Rāma and Śaṃbhu, / that should be known as a field of the perfected, [extending] three yojanas on all sides.

2.43.s:
tīrthe na pratigṛhṇīyātpuṇyeṣvāyataneṣu ca /
nimitteṣu ca sarveṣu tannivṛtto bhavennaraḥ //
2.43.d:
तीर्थे न प्रतिगृह्णीयात्पुण्येष्वायतनेषु च ।
निमित्तेषु च सर्वेषु तन्निवृत्तो भवेन्नरः ॥
2.43.m: One should not accept gifts at a sacred ford or in holy temples; / and on all occasions, a man should abstain from that.

2.43.s:
tīrthe yaḥ pratigṛhṇāti puṇyeṣvāyataneṣu ca /
niṣphalaṃ tasya tattīrthaṃ yāvattaddhanamucyate //
2.43.d:
तीर्थे यः प्रतिगृह्णाति पुण्येष्वायतनेषु च ।
निष्फलं तस्य तत्तीर्थं यावत्तद्धनमुच्यते ॥
2.43.m: Whoever accepts gifts at a sacred ford and in holy temples, / that sacred ford becomes fruitless for him so long as that wealth is spoken of.

2.43.s:
gaṅgāvikrayāṇāddevi viṣṇorvikrayaṇaṃ bhavet /
janārdane tu vikrīte vikrītaṃ bhuvanatrayam //
2.43.d:
गङ्गाविक्रयाणाद्देवि विष्णोर्विक्रयणं भवेत् ।
जनार्दने तु विक्रीते विक्रीतं भुवनत्रयम् ॥
2.43.m: O goddess, from selling the Gaṅgā comes the sale of Viṣṇu; / and when Janārdana is sold, the three worlds are sold.

2.43.s:
gaṅgā tīrasamudbhūtāṃ ma-daṃ mūrghnā bibharti yaḥ /
bibharti rūpaṃ sor'kasya tamonāśāya kevalam //
2.43.d:
गङ्गा तीरसमुद्भूतां म-दं मूर्घ्ना बिभर्ति यः ।
बिभर्ति रूपं सोर्ऽकस्य तमोनाशाय केवलम् ॥
2.43.m: Whoever bears on his head the clay originating from the bank of the Gaṅgā / bears the very form of the sun solely to destroy darkness.

2.43.s:
gaṅgāpulinajāṃ dhūlimāstīryātha nijān pitṝn /
prīṇayanyo naraḥ piṇḍāndadyāttān svarnayedapi //
2.43.d:
गङ्गापुलिनजां धूलिमास्तीर्याथ निजान् पितॄन् ।
प्रीणयन्यो नरः पिण्डान्दद्यात्तान् स्वर्नयेदपि ॥
2.43.m: Having spread the sand produced on the sandbanks of the Gaṅgā, the man / who, pleasing his ancestors, offers piṇḍas leads them to heaven.

2.43.s:
idaṃ te 'bhihitaṃ bhadre gaṅgāmāhātmyamuttamam /
paṭhan śṛṇvannaro hyeti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam //
2.43.d:
इदं ते ऽभिहितं भद्रे गङ्गामाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ।
पठन् शृण्वन्नरो ह्येति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
2.43.m: This supreme eulogy of the greatness of the Gaṅgā has been declared to you, O auspicious lady; / reading or hearing it, a man indeed goes to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

2.43.s:
nityaṃ japyamidaṃ bhaktyā prayataiḥ śraddhayānvitaiḥ /
vaiṣṇavīṃ gatimicchadbhiḥ śaivīṃ vā vidhinandini //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge mohinīvasusaṃvāde gaṅgāmāhātmye pūjādikathaṃ nāma tricatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.43.d:
नित्यं जप्यमिदं भक्त्या प्रयतैः श्रद्धयान्वितैः ।
वैष्णवीं गतिमिच्छद्भिः शैवीं वा विधिनन्दिनि ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे मोहिनीवसुसंवादे गङ्गामाहात्म्ये पूजादिकथं नाम त्रिचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
2.43.m:
This is to be recited constantly with devotion by the restrained and endowed with faith, / who desire the state of Viṣṇu or that of Śiva, O daughter of the Ordainer.

Thus ends the forty-third chapter, named 'The Account of Worship and Other Matters in the Eulogy of the Greatness of the Gaṅgā', in the dialogue between Mohinī and Vasu, in the latter section of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.
